```{r}
theme_dracula <- function(base_size = 13) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "#282a36", colour = NA),
          panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#282a36", colour = NA),
          panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "#44475a"),
          panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
          text = element_text(colour = "#f8f8f2"), axis.text = element_text(colour = "#f8f8f2"),
          legend.background = element_rect(fill = "#282a36", colour = NA),
          legend.key = element_rect(fill = "#282a36", colour = NA),
          plot.title = element_text(colour = "#bd93f9", face = "bold"))
}
theme_set(theme_dracula())
options(ggplot2.discrete.fill = c("#8be9fd", "#ff79c6"),
        ggplot2.discrete.colour = c("#8be9fd", "#ff79c6"),
        width = 110, digits = 3)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(dev = "png", dpi = 150, fig.align = "center")

# Recolour every ggplot for the dark slides (cobalt plots use their own white theme).
# Plots flagged with attr "keep_theme" (diagrams) are printed untouched.
dr_cols <- theme(
  plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#282a36", colour = NA),
  panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#282a36", colour = NA),
  panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "#44475a"), panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),

  axis.text = element_text(colour = "#f8f8f2"), axis.text.x = element_text(colour = "#f8f8f2"),
  axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "#f8f8f2"), axis.title = element_text(colour = "#f8f8f2"),
  axis.ticks = element_line(colour = "#6272a4"),
  legend.text = element_text(colour = "#f8f8f2"), legend.title = element_text(colour = "#f8f8f2"),
  legend.background = element_rect(fill = "#282a36", colour = NA),
  legend.key = element_rect(fill = "#282a36", colour = NA),

  plot.title = element_text(colour = "#bd93f9", face = "bold"),
  plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "#8be9fd"))
registerS3method("knit_print", "ggplot", function(x, ...) {
  if (!isTRUE(attr(x, "keep_theme"))) x <- if (inherits(x, "patchwork")) x & dr_cols else x + dr_cols
  print(x); invisible(NULL)
}, envir = asNamespace("knitr"))

# Dark styling for gt / gtsummary tables
style_gt_dark <- function(x) {
  gt::tab_options(x, table.background.color = "#282a36", table.font.color = "#f8f8f2",
                  column_labels.background.color = "#44475a", table.font.size = gt::px(13),
                  data_row.padding = gt::px(2), table.border.top.color = "#6272a4",
                  table.border.bottom.color = "#6272a4", column_labels.border.bottom.color = "#bd93f9",
                  row_group.background.color = "#44475a", footnotes.font.size = gt::px(11),
                  source_notes.font.size = gt::px(11), heading.background.color = "#44475a",
                  table.width = gt::pct(100))
}
gt_knit_print <- getS3method("knit_print", "gt_tbl", envir = asNamespace("knitr"))
registerS3method("knit_print", "gt_tbl",
                 function(x, ...) gt_knit_print(style_gt_dark(x), ...), envir = asNamespace("knitr"))
registerS3method("knit_print", "gtsummary",
                 function(x, ...) gt_knit_print(style_gt_dark(gtsummary::as_gt(x)), ...), envir = asNamespace("knitr"))


# Slide-display version of a Love plot: top-n covariates only, so labels stay readable
love_top <- function(bal, n = 25, labels = c("Before", "After")) {
  bal$Balance |>
    rownames_to_column("covariate") |>
    filter(covariate != "distance", covariate != "prop.score") |>
    slice_max(abs(Diff.Un), n = n) |>
    mutate(covariate = fct_reorder(covariate, abs(Diff.Un))) |>
    pivot_longer(c(Diff.Un, Diff.Adj), names_to = "sample", values_to = "smd") |>
    mutate(sample = factor(if_else(sample == "Diff.Un", labels[1], labels[2]), levels = labels)) |>
    ggplot(aes(abs(smd), covariate, colour = sample, shape = sample)) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = 0.1, linetype = 2, colour = "#ffb86c") +
    geom_point(size = 2.5) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("#ff5555", "#50fa7b")) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = c(16, 17)) +
    labs(x = "Absolute standardized mean difference", y = NULL, colour = NULL, shape = NULL,
         title = paste("Covariate balance:", n, "most imbalanced terms")) +
    theme(legend.position = "top")
}

# Causal diagram helper (no axes, no grid, no special characters)
draw_dag <- function(nodes, edges, title) {
  e <- merge(merge(edges, nodes, by.x = "from", by.y = "id"), nodes,
             by.x = "to", by.y = "id", suffixes = c("", "_to"))
  dx <- e$x_to - e$x; dy <- e$y_to - e$y
  e$x <- e$x + 0.22 * dx; e$y <- e$y + 0.22 * dy
  e$x_to <- e$x_to - 0.22 * dx; e$y_to <- e$y_to - 0.22 * dy
  ggplot() +
    geom_segment(data = subset(e, lty == "solid"), aes(x = x, y = y, xend = x_to, yend = y_to),
                 arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.25, "cm"), type = "closed"), colour = "#f8f8f2", linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_segment(data = subset(e, lty == "blocked"), aes(x = x, y = y, xend = x_to, yend = y_to),
                 linetype = 2, colour = "#ff5555", linewidth = 0.8) +
    geom_label(data = nodes, aes(x, y, label = label), fill = "#44475a", colour = "#f8f8f2",
               label.size = 0, size = 4.2, label.padding = unit(0.4, "lines")) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.5, y = 1.22, label = title, colour = "#bd93f9", size = 5.5, fontface = "bold") +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-0.15, 1.15), ylim = c(-0.15, 1.3)) +
    theme_void() + theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#282a36", colour = NA))
}

# Simulated teaching data file (created once if not supplied)
if (!file.exists("sim_severity.csv")) {
  set.seed(2026)
  n <- 5000
  tibble(id = 1:n, severity = round(rnorm(n), 3)) |>
    mutate(treated = rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-0.5 + 1.5 * severity)),
           died    = rbinom(n, 1, plogis(-1.0 + 1.2 * severity))) |>
    write_csv("sim_severity.csv")
}
```

## The clinical question · 임상적 질문 (1/2)

**Right heart catheterization (RHC)** — the *pulmonary artery* or *Swan-Ganz* catheter

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
**What it is · 무엇인가**

- A catheter passed through a large vein and the right heart into the **pulmonary artery**
- Measures heart pressures and **cardiac output** at the bedside

**Why ICU doctors used it · 사용 이유**

- In shock, respiratory failure, or heart failure, it is hard to judge: *more fluid, or drugs to support the heart and blood pressure?*
- RHC measurements were thought to **guide these treatment decisions** better than the bedside exam
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
**Risks · 위험**

- Arrhythmias, infection, bleeding, lung injury
- Measurements can be **misread** → wrong treatment

**The problem (1980s–90s) · 문제점**

- Widely used, but **never tested in a randomized trial**
- Many clinicians were sure it helped → withholding it in a trial felt **unethical**
:::
::::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**우심도자술(RHC)**: 폐동맥까지 카테터를 넣어 심장 압력과 심박출량을 측정하는 시술. 치료 결정에 도움이 된다고 믿었지만 **무작위 임상시험 근거는 없었습니다**.
:::

## The clinical question · 임상적 질문 (2/2)

**Connors et al., *JAMA* 1996**: *In critically ill ICU patients, is RHC in the first 24 hours associated with survival?*

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
**Data · 자료**

- **SUPPORT** study: 5 US teaching hospitals, 1989–1994
- **5,735** critically ill adults
- Detailed day-1 data, like an **EHR extract**: diagnoses, APACHE III severity score, vital signs, labs, comorbidities

**Findings · 결과**

- Propensity score matching (1,006 pairs): **30-day mortality odds ratio 1.24** (95% CI 1.03–1.49) for RHC
- Later RCTs (PAC-Man 2005, ESCAPE 2005, FACTT 2006) found **no benefit** from routine RHC
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Think · 생각해보기 (2 min)"}
1. Which patients were more likely to get RHC: the most stable or the sickest?
2. If sicker patients get RHC *and* die more often, what will a simple comparison of death rates show?
:::
:::
::::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
관찰 자료로 RHC의 효과를 추정한 연구입니다. 핵심 문제: **더 위중한 환자가 RHC를 받았다**는 점입니다. 원 연구 결과: 30일 사망 **오즈비 1.24**.
:::

## Step 0 · Load all packages · 패키지 불러오기

All packages are loaded **once**, at the top of the starter script.

```{r}
#| label: load-packages
library(tidyverse)        # dplyr, ggplot2, readr, ...
library(MatchIt)          # matchit(), match.data()
library(optmatch)         # optimal / full matching
library(cobalt)           # bal.tab(), love.plot(), bal.plot()
library(gtsummary)        # tbl_summary(), tbl_svysummary(), tbl_merge()
library(gt)               # table rendering
library(survey)           # svydesign() for weighted tables
library(smd)              # standardized mean differences (used by add_smd())
library(marginaleffects)  # avg_comparisons()
library(sandwich)         # robust variance
library(broom)            # tidy()
library(patchwork)        # p1 + p2
library(EValue)           # evalues.RR()
library(scales)           # percent()
set.seed(2026)
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
Messages such as *"Attaching package"* or *"objects are masked"* are **normal**. An error such as *"there is no package called 'xxx'"* means the package is not installed.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
모든 패키지를 **처음에 한 번** 불러옵니다. "masked" 메시지는 오류가 아닙니다.
:::

## Step 0 · Prepare the RHC data · 자료 준비

Also in the starter script:

```{r}
#| label: data
url <- "https://hbiostat.org/data/repo/rhc.csv"
if (!file.exists("rhc.csv")) download.file(url, destfile = "rhc.csv")
rhc <- read.csv("rhc.csv")

rhc <- rhc |>
  mutate(
    treat  = as.integer(swang1 == "RHC"),   # treatment: 1 = RHC, 0 = no RHC
    died30 = as.integer(dth30  == "Yes"),   # outcome: 1 = died within 30 days
    swang1 = factor(swang1, levels = c("No RHC", "RHC")),
    across(c(cat1, ca, sex, race, income, ninsclas, dnr1, resp, card, neuro,
             gastr, renal, meta, hema, seps, trauma, ortho), factor)
  )

# The 50 baseline covariates used by Connors et al.
covs <- c("age","sex","race","edu","income","ninsclas","cat1","das2d3pc","dnr1",
          "ca","surv2md1","aps1","scoma1","wtkilo1","temp1","meanbp1","resp1",
          "hrt1","pafi1","paco21","ph1","wblc1","hema1","sod1","pot1","crea1",
          "bili1","alb1","resp","card","neuro","gastr","renal","meta","hema",
          "seps","trauma","ortho","cardiohx","chfhx","dementhx","psychhx",
          "chrpulhx","renalhx","liverhx","gibledhx","malighx","immunhx",
          "transhx","amihx")
```

## Step 0 · A helper for Table 1 · 기초특성표 도우미 함수

Also in the starter script. **gtsummary** cannot show p-values and standardized mean differences (SMD) side by side on its own, so we add one small function, `add_smd()`.

```{r}
#| label: add-smd
#| code-fold: false
# Adds an SMD column to a gtsummary table (tbl_summary or tbl_svysummary)
add_smd <- function(tbl) {
  smd_fun <- function(data, variable, by, ...) {
    w <- NULL
    if (inherits(data, "survey.design")) { w <- weights(data); data <- data$variables }
    tibble::tibble(smd = smd::smd(x = data[[variable]], g = data[[by]], w = w)$estimate)
  }
  tbl |>
    add_stat(fns = everything() ~ smd_fun) |>
    modify_header(smd ~ "**SMD**") |>
    modify_fmt_fun(smd ~ label_style_number(digits = 2))
}
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
Use it at the end of a gtsummary pipe: `tbl_summary(...) |> add_p() |> add_smd()`. You do not need to understand its internals. If the SMD column is empty, the **smd** package is not installed.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
`add_smd()`는 기초특성표에 **표준화 평균차이(SMD)** 열을 추가하는 도우미 함수입니다. 시작 스크립트에 포함되어 있습니다.
:::

## Step 0 · Results · 결과

```{r}
#| label: data-explore-out
#| echo: false
dim(rhc)
count(rhc, swang1)
mean(rhc$died30)
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- **`r nrow(rhc)` patients** (one row per ICU admission) and `r ncol(rhc)` variables.
- `aps1` and `pafi1` are numeric; `cat1` (primary diagnosis) is a **factor**.
- **`r sum(rhc$treat == 1)`** patients received RHC (`r percent(mean(rhc$treat), 0.1)`); `r sum(rhc$treat == 0)` did not.
- **`r percent(mean(rhc$died30), 0.1)`** died within 30 days. The mean of a 0/1 variable is a **proportion**.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
환자 `r nrow(rhc)`명 중 `r percent(mean(rhc$treat), 0.1)`가 RHC를 받았고, `r percent(mean(rhc$died30), 0.1)`가 30일 이내 사망했습니다.
:::

# Part 1 · Why propensity scores? {background-color="#44475a"}

왜 성향점수가 필요한가?

## EHR data: a goldmine with traps

**전자건강기록(EHR): 보물창고, 그러나 함정이 있다**

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Strengths · 장점
- **Large** — thousands to millions of patients
- **Real-world** patients, including those excluded from trials
- Rich detail: labs, vitals, diagnoses, medications
- Long follow-up at low cost
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
### Problems · 문제점
- Collected **for care, not research**
- Treatment is chosen by clinicians → **not random**
- Missing data and coding errors
- Time-related biases
:::
::::

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Think–pair · 생각해보기 (2 min)"}
Name one treatment in your hospital that *sicker* patients are more likely to receive. What would a simple comparison of outcomes show?
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
EHR에서 치료는 의사가 환자 상태를 보고 결정하므로 **무작위가 아닙니다** → 단순 비교는 편향될 수 있습니다.
:::

## RCT vs. observational EHR study

**무작위 대조 시험(RCT) vs. 관찰연구**

```{r}
#| label: dags
#| echo: false
#| out-width: 100%
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 3.4
nodes <- data.frame(id = c("C", "S", "A", "Y"), x = c(0, 0.5, 0, 1), y = c(1, 0.95, 0.1, 0.1),
                    label = c("Coin flip", "Severity", "Treatment", "Death"))
e_rct <- data.frame(from = c("C", "A", "S", "S"), to = c("A", "Y", "Y", "A"),
                    lty = c("solid", "solid", "solid", "blocked"))
e_ehr <- data.frame(from = c("S", "A", "S"), to = c("A", "Y", "Y"), lty = "solid")
n_ehr <- subset(nodes, id != "C"); n_ehr$label[n_ehr$id == "A"] <- "Treatment\n(doctor's choice)"
p_dag <- draw_dag(nodes, e_rct, "Randomized trial (RCT)") + draw_dag(n_ehr, e_ehr, "Observational (EHR)")
attr(p_dag, "keep_theme") <- TRUE
p_dag
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- Arrows mean "causes". **RCT (left):** a coin flip decides treatment, so severity cannot influence it (red dashed line = arrow removed).
- **EHR (right):** severity causes **both** treatment and death. Severity is a **confounder**: treated patients may die more even if the treatment does nothing.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**적응증에 의한 교란**: 위중한 환자일수록 치료를 받을 확률도, 사망 위험도 높습니다. 치료 효과와 중증도 효과가 **섞입니다**.
:::

## Simulation 1 · Compare death by treatment · 사망률 비교

`sim_severity.csv` contains 5,000 **simulated** ICU patients where we know the truth:

- `severity` (higher = sicker), `treated` (1 = yes), `died` (1 = yes)
- Sicker patients were more likely to be treated **and** more likely to die
- The treatment has **no effect** on death

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (4 min)"}
1. Read the file into an object `sim`. *(`read_csv()`)*
2. Compute the proportion who died among treated and untreated patients. *(`group_by()`, `summarise()`)*
:::

```{r}
#| label: sim-compare
#| output: false
sim <- read_csv("sim_severity.csv")
sim_by_trt <- sim |>
  group_by(treated) |>
  summarise(n = n(), risk_of_death = mean(died))
sim_by_trt
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
치료 효과가 **0**인 가상 자료입니다. 치료군과 비치료군의 사망 비율을 비교해 보세요.
:::

## Simulation 1 · Results · 결과

```{r}
#| label: sim-compare-out
#| echo: false
sim_by_trt
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- **`r percent(sim_by_trt$risk_of_death[2], 0.1)`** of treated patients died vs **`r percent(sim_by_trt$risk_of_death[1], 0.1)`** of untreated patients — about **`r round(sim_by_trt$risk_of_death[2] / sim_by_trt$risk_of_death[1], 1)` times** as high.
- Yet the treatment does **nothing**. The treated patients were simply **sicker**.
- This is **confounding**: the comparison mixes the effect of treatment with the effect of severity.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
효과가 없는 치료인데도 치료군 사망률이 약 `r round(sim_by_trt$risk_of_death[2] / sim_by_trt$risk_of_death[1], 1)`배 높습니다 → **교란** 때문입니다.
:::

## Simulation 2 · Compare within severity groups · 중증도별 비교

Idea: compare treated and untreated patients **who are equally sick**.

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (6 min)"}
1. Divide `severity` into **5 equal-sized groups** (1 = mildest, 5 = sickest). *(`ntile()`)*
2. Compute the risk of death for each severity group **and** treatment group. Save as `sim_q`.
3. Plot risk of death (y) against severity group (x), with **one line per treatment group**. Save as `p_sim`. *(`ggplot()`, `geom_line()`, `geom_point()`)*
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="💡 Hint · 힌트"}
Treat `treated` as a factor so that ggplot draws two separate lines with different colours.
:::

```{r}
#| label: sim-strata
#| output: false
sim_q <- sim |>
  mutate(severity_q = ntile(severity, 5)) |>
  group_by(severity_q, treated) |>
  summarise(n = n(), risk = mean(died), .groups = "drop")
sim_q

p_sim <- ggplot(sim_q, aes(x = severity_q, y = risk, colour = factor(treated))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_point(size = 3) +
  labs(x = "Severity group (1 = mildest, 5 = sickest)", y = "Risk of death",
       colour = "Treated", title = "Risk of death by severity and treatment")
p_sim
```

## Simulation 2 · Results · 결과

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="38%"}
```{r}
#| label: sim-strata-out
#| echo: false
sim_q |> mutate(risk = round(risk, 2))
```
:::
::: {.column width="62%"}
```{r}
#| label: sim-plot-out
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 3.1
p_sim
```
:::
::::

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- Risk of death rises steeply with severity, but within each severity group the two lines **almost coincide** → no treatment effect, the truth we built in.
- The group sizes (`n`) show why the crude comparison misled: mild groups are mostly untreated, severe groups mostly treated.
- With **one** confounder, stratifying is easy. The RHC data have **50** — the propensity score handles them all at once.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**같은 중증도끼리** 비교하면 차이가 사라집니다. 성향점수는 이런 비교를 **많은 변수에 대해 한 번에** 합니다.
:::

## Why not just adjust in a regression? · 회귀모형으로 보정하면 안 되나요?

You can, and the best analyses often combine both. But regression alone has limitations:

| Issue | Outcome regression | Propensity score methods |
|---|---|---|
| Many confounders, few outcome events | Risk of overfitting | Models *treatment*, often more common than the outcome |
| Treated and untreated patients with **little overlap in characteristics** | Extrapolates from the model, without warning | PS plots show where comparable patients are missing |
| Was confounding removed? | No direct check; relies on a correct model | Check covariate balance (SMD, Love plot) |
| Revising the analysis | Can be pre-specified, but checking or changing the model means refitting with the outcome | Check and revise using only treatment and covariates; outcome used once, at the end |

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
Regression can also be pre-specified without seeing outcomes. The advantage of propensity scores is that the *design* can be checked and improved before the outcome is used, as in an RCT. Neither approach handles **unmeasured** confounding.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
성향점수 방법은 결과를 사용하기 **전에** 중첩과 균형을 확인하고 설계를 개선할 수 있습니다.
:::

## Exact matching 1 · One and three variables · 정확 매칭

**Exact matching** groups RHC and non-RHC patients who have **identical** values on the chosen variables; patients in a group with no one from the other treatment group are dropped. How far does it get us?

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (5 min)"}
1. Exact-match on **sex** only. *(`matchit()` with `method = "exact"`)*
2. What percentage of the `r sum(rhc$treat)` RHC patients found a match? *(`summary()`, element `$nn`)*
3. Repeat with **sex + `cat1` + `dnr1`**.
:::

```{r}
#| label: exact-1-3
#| output: false
ex1 <- matchit(treat ~ sex, data = rhc, method = "exact")
summary(ex1)$nn
pct1 <- summary(ex1)$nn["Matched", "Treated"] / sum(rhc$treat)

ex3 <- matchit(treat ~ sex + cat1 + dnr1, data = rhc, method = "exact")
summary(ex3)$nn
pct3 <- summary(ex3)$nn["Matched", "Treated"] / sum(rhc$treat)
c(pct1, pct3)
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**정확 매칭**: 선택한 변수의 값이 **완전히 같은** 환자끼리 묶습니다. 변수 1개, 3개로 해 보세요.
:::

## Exact matching 1 · Results: reading `summary()` · 결과 읽기

```{r}
#| label: exact-1-summary
#| echo: false
s1 <- summary(ex1)
round(s1$sum.all[, c("Means Treated", "Means Control", "Std. Mean Diff.", "eCDF Max")], 3)
round(s1$sum.matched[, c("Means Treated", "Means Control", "Std. Mean Diff.", "Std. Pair Dist.")], 3)
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- **Rows:** `sex` is a factor, so each level gets a 0/1 indicator. The **mean of a 0/1 variable is a proportion**: `r percent(s1$sum.all["sexFemale", "Means Treated"], 0.1)` of RHC patients vs `r percent(s1$sum.all["sexFemale", "Means Control"], 0.1)` of controls are female.
- **Std. Mean Diff.** (SMD): `r sprintf("%.3f", s1$sum.all["sexFemale", "Std. Mean Diff."])` before matching — just under 0.1. MatchIt divides by the **RHC group's SD**, because the target population is the RHC patients (the ATT, defined later). **eCDF Max:** the largest gap between the two distributions; for a 0/1 variable it equals the difference in proportions.
- **After matching**, the proportions are identical and every statistic is 0 (`-0` is rounding). **Std. Pair Dist.** = average difference within matched groups: 0, because patients match exactly. `Var. Ratio` (not shown) is blank for binary variables.
- **Why did the control mean change?** Exact matching keeps **everyone** in a group and **re-weights the controls** so they mirror the RHC group (e.g., female controls get a slightly smaller weight).
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
0/1 변수의 평균 = **비율**. 정확 매칭은 대조군에 **가중치**를 주어 RHC군과 같은 비율이 되게 합니다. 매칭 후 SMD = 0.
:::

## Exact matching 1 · Results: sample sizes · 표본 크기

```{r}
#| label: exact-nn
#| echo: false
nn1 <- summary(ex1)$nn; nn3 <- summary(ex3)$nn
nn1
nn3
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- **Sex only** (first table): every patient is matched — all `r sum(rhc$treat)` RHC patients and all `r sum(rhc$treat == 0)` controls.
- **Sex + `cat1` + `dnr1`** (second table): still **all RHC patients** matched. **`r nn3["Unmatched", "Control"]` controls** are unmatched: they belong to a combination (e.g., men with lung cancer and a DNR order) that **no RHC patient** has, so there is no one to compare them with.
- **ESS** (effective sample size) = $(\sum w)^2 / \sum w^2$. The `r nn3["Matched", "Control"]` matched controls carry **unequal weights** (large where there are many RHC patients per control, e.g., sepsis; small where there are few, e.g., COPD), so they are worth only about **`r round(nn3["Matched (ESS)", "Control"])`** equally weighted patients. Lower ESS = less information = wider confidence intervals.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
변수 3개: RHC 환자는 모두 매칭, 대조군 `r nn3["Unmatched", "Control"]`명은 같은 조합의 RHC 환자가 없어 제외. **유효 표본 크기(ESS)**는 가중치가 불균등할수록 작아집니다.
:::

## Exact matching 2 · Ten variables · 변수 10개

Continuous variables almost never match exactly, so first cut them into **quintiles** (5 groups).

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (5 min)"}
1. Create quintile versions of `age`, `aps1`, `meanbp1`, `pafi1`, `crea1` in a new data set `rhc_q`. *(`ntile()`)*
2. Exact-match on 10 variables: `sex`, `cat1`, `dnr1`, `ca`, `race`, plus your 5 quintile variables.
3. What percentage of RHC patients found a match now?
:::

```{r}
#| label: exact-10
#| output: false
rhc_q <- rhc |>
  mutate(age_q = ntile(age, 5), aps_q = ntile(aps1, 5), bp_q = ntile(meanbp1, 5),
         pafi_q = ntile(pafi1, 5), crea_q = ntile(crea1, 5))
ex10 <- matchit(treat ~ sex + cat1 + dnr1 + ca + race + age_q + aps_q + bp_q + pafi_q + crea_q,
                data = rhc_q, method = "exact")
summary(ex10)$nn
pct10 <- summary(ex10)$nn["Matched", "Treated"] / sum(rhc$treat)
pct10
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
연속형 변수는 5분위로 나눈 뒤, 10개 변수로 정확 매칭해 보세요.
:::

## Exact matching · Results: the curse of dimensionality · 차원의 저주

```{r}
#| label: exact-all
#| echo: false
ex_vars <- c("sex", "cat1", "dnr1", "ca", "race", "age_q", "aps_q", "bp_q", "pafi_q", "crea_q")
pct_curve <- map_dbl(seq_along(ex_vars), function(k) {
  m <- matchit(reformulate(ex_vars[1:k], "treat"), data = rhc_q, method = "exact")
  summary(m)$nn["Matched", "Treated"] / sum(rhc_q$treat)
})
```

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
```{r}
#| label: exact-plot
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6.2
#| fig-height: 3.0
tibble(k = seq_along(ex_vars), pct = pct_curve, var = ex_vars) |>
  ggplot(aes(k, pct)) +
  geom_line(colour = "#ff79c6", linewidth = 1.2) + geom_point(colour = "#ff79c6", size = 3) +
  geom_point(data = tibble(k = c(1, 3, 10), pct = c(pct1, pct3, pct10)),
             colour = "#50fa7b", size = 5, shape = 21, stroke = 1.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = var), vjust = -1.1, size = 3, colour = "#f8f8f2") +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent, limits = c(0, 1.1)) + scale_x_continuous(breaks = 1:10) +
  labs(x = "Number of variables matched exactly", y = "RHC patients matched",
       title = "Exact matching in the RHC data")
```
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
| Variables | RHC patients matched |
|---|---|
| 1 | **`r percent(pct1, 1)`** |
| 3 | **`r percent(pct3, 1)`** |
| 10 | **`r percent(pct10, 1)`** |
:::
::::

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- With 1 or 3 variables, nearly every RHC patient finds an identical control. With **10**, only **`r percent(pct10, 1)`** do — the rest would be discarded. Green circles = your exercises.
- With **50** covariates, exact matching is impossible: the **curse of dimensionality**.
- Solution: summarize all covariates in **one number**, the propensity score, and match on that.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
변수가 많아지면 똑같은 환자를 찾을 수 없습니다 (**차원의 저주**). 그래서 모든 변수를 **하나의 점수**로 요약합니다.
:::

## Exact matching · What does a match look like? · 정확 매칭의 예

Patients in the same exact-matching group share **sex, `cat1`, and `dnr1`**. Here are a few from one group (male, MOSF with sepsis, no DNR order):

```{r}
#| label: exact-rows
#| echo: false
md3 <- match.data(ex3)
grp <- md3 |> filter(sex == "Male", cat1 == "MOSF w/Sepsis", dnr1 == "No")
set.seed(7)
ex_rows <- bind_rows(slice_sample(filter(grp, treat == 1), n = 3),
                     slice_sample(filter(grp, treat == 0), n = 3)) |>
  transmute(Group = if_else(treat == 1, "RHC", "No RHC"), sex, cat1, dnr1,
            Age = round(age), `APACHE III` = aps1, `Mean BP` = meanbp1, `PaO2/FiO2` = round(pafi1))
ex_rows |>
  gt() |>
  tab_style(style = cell_text(color = "#50fa7b", weight = "bold"),
            locations = cells_body(columns = c(sex, cat1, dnr1))) |>
  tab_style(style = cell_text(color = "#ff79c6", weight = "bold"),
            locations = cells_body(columns = c(Age, `APACHE III`, `Mean BP`, `PaO2/FiO2`)))
```

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (3 min)"}
Extract the matched data from `ex3` (`match.data()`) and look at a few RHC and non-RHC patients in one `subclass`. Which variables are identical? Which are not?
:::

```{r}
#| label: exact-rows-solution
#| output: false
md3 <- match.data(ex3)
md3 |>
  filter(subclass == 2) |>
  group_by(swang1) |>
  slice_head(n = 3) |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(subclass, swang1, weights, sex, cat1, dnr1, age, aps1, meanbp1, pafi1)
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- **Green:** identical within the group — these are the matching variables.
- **Pink:** age, severity (APACHE III), blood pressure, and oxygenation still differ a lot. Matching exactly on 3 variables leaves the other 47 unbalanced, and matching exactly on all 50 is impossible.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
매칭 변수(초록)는 같지만 나이·중증도·혈압·산소화(분홍)는 여전히 크게 다릅니다. 변수 3개로는 나머지 47개의 균형을 맞출 수 없습니다.
:::

## What is a propensity score? · 성향점수란?

$$
e(X) = \Pr(\text{Treatment} = 1 \mid X)
$$

The probability that a patient receives the treatment, **given their measured covariates** X (Rosenbaum & Rubin, 1983).

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
**Balancing property · 균형 성질**

Patients with the **same PS** have, on average, the **same distribution of X**, whether or not they were treated.

So, within PS-matched pairs, treatment is *as if* randomized — but **only with respect to measured X**.
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
**Ways to use a PS · 활용법**

1. **Matching** ← today
2. **Weighting (IPTW)** ← today
3. Stratification
4. Covariate adjustment
:::
::::

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Check yourself · 확인 (1 min)"}
A patient has PS = 0.05. What does that mean in words? Would you expect many such patients in the RHC group?
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**성향점수** = 측정된 공변량이 주어졌을 때 치료를 받을 확률. 성향점수가 같은 환자들은 공변량 분포가 비슷합니다 (**균형 성질**).
:::

## Key assumptions · 핵심 가정

| Assumption | Meaning | In the RHC study |
|---|---|---|
| **Exchangeability** (교환가능성) | No unmeasured confounding | Is the doctor's impression of "how sick" in the data? |
| **Positivity** (양수성) | Every type of patient could receive either treatment | Some patients would never get RHC (e.g., comfort care) |
| **Consistency** (일치성) | The treatment is well defined | Is "RHC within 24 h" the same everywhere? |
| **Correct PS model** | The model captures who gets treated | Judged by **balance**, not fit statistics |

::: {.callout-important title="PS ≠ magic · 성향점수는 마법이 아닙니다"}
Propensity scores balance only **measured** covariates. Unmeasured confounding remains possible → we will do a **sensitivity analysis** at the end.
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Discuss · 토론 (2 min)"}
Name one **unmeasured** factor that could affect both the decision to place an RHC and the risk of death.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
성향점수는 **측정된** 공변량만 균형을 맞춥니다. 교환가능성, 양수성, 일치성은 자료로 완전히 검증할 수 없습니다.
:::

## What effect are we estimating? · 추정 대상 (estimand)

The **estimand** is the exact quantity we want to estimate. Two are common:

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**ATE — Average Treatment Effect** · 평균처치효과

The average effect of RHC **in all patients** in the study population.

*Compare:* a world where **every** patient gets RHC vs a world where **no** patient gets RHC.
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**ATT — Average Treatment effect in the Treated** · 처치군 평균처치효과

The average effect of RHC **in the patients who actually received RHC**.

*Compare:* what happened to RHC patients vs what **would have happened to the same patients** without RHC.
:::
::::

**Potential outcomes:** each patient has two possible outcomes, $Y^1$ (with RHC) and $Y^0$ (without). We only ever observe one of them, so the other must be estimated from comparable patients.

$$
\text{ATE} = E[Y^1 - Y^0] \qquad\qquad \text{ATT} = E[Y^1 - Y^0 \mid \text{received RHC}]
$$

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- ATE and ATT differ when the effect differs between the kinds of patients who get treated and those who don't. E.g., if RHC harms the sickest most, and RHC patients are sicker, the ATT shows more harm than the ATE.
- **Matching** treated patients to controls estimates the **ATT**. **IPTW** (with 1/PS weights) estimates the **ATE**.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**ATE** = 모든 환자가 치료받은 경우와 아무도 받지 않은 경우의 평균 차이. **ATT** = 실제로 치료받은 환자에서, 치료를 받은 경우와 받지 않았을 경우의 평균 차이.
:::

## ATE or ATT: which do we want? · 어떤 것을 선택할까?

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Choose the ATT when… · ATT**

- The question is about patients who **currently receive** the treatment: *"Is RHC helping or harming the patients we place it in?"*
- Many untreated patients would **never** be candidates (e.g., mild illness, comfort care) — so "treat everyone" is not a realistic policy
- Typical for **matching**
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Choose the ATE when… · ATE**

- The question is a **policy for everyone**: *"Should all ICU patients like these receive RHC?"*
- Every patient type could realistically receive either option (positivity holds for all)
- Typical for **IPTW** and outcome regression
:::
::::

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
For RHC, the **ATT** is the more natural question: RHC is given to selected, unstable patients, and nobody proposes placing it in every ICU patient. We will estimate both and compare.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**ATT**: "현재 치료받는 환자에게 도움이 되는가?" **ATE**: "모든 환자에게 적용해야 하는가?" RHC 연구에서는 **ATT**가 더 자연스러운 질문입니다.
:::

## Positivity · 양수성

**Definition** (Westreich & Cole, 2010): there must be both treated **and** untreated patients at every combination of the confounders — formally, $0 < \Pr(\text{treatment} \mid X) < 1$.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Two kinds of violation · 두 가지 위반**

- **Structural:** some patients *cannot* receive one option (e.g., RHC contraindicated, comfort care). More data does not help.
- **Random (practical):** treatment was possible, but by chance few or no patients of that type received it (or did not).
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Which end of the PS matters? · 어느 쪽이 중요한가**

- **ATT (matching):** every *treated* patient needs comparable controls → problems at the **high-PS** end.
- **ATE (IPTW):** every patient needs comparable patients in *both* groups → problems at **both ends**.
:::
::::

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
A positivity problem means that, for some types of patients, the data contain **no information** about what would have happened under the other option. We will see it in the overlap plot (Step 2) and in the IPTW weights (Step 6).
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**양수성**: 모든 공변량 조합에 치료군과 비치료군이 모두 있어야 합니다. 매칭(ATT)은 성향점수가 **높은** 쪽, IPTW(ATE)는 **양쪽 끝** 모두가 중요합니다.
:::

## Measuring the effect · 효과 척도: RD, RR, OR

For a yes/no outcome with risk $p_1$ (treated) and $p_0$ (untreated). Example: $p_1 = 0.38$, $p_0 = 0.31$.

| Measure | Formula | Example | Say it as |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Risk difference (RD)** 위험차 | $p_1 - p_0$ | **0.07** | "7 **percentage points** higher" (absolute) |
| **Risk ratio (RR)** 위험비 | $p_1 / p_0$ | **1.23** | "23% higher" (relative) |
| **Odds ratio (OR)** 오즈비 | $\frac{p_1/(1-p_1)}{p_0/(1-p_0)}$ | **1.36** | "1.36 times the odds" |

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- **No effect:** RD = 0, RR = 1, OR = 1.
- **Percentage points ≠ percent:** 31% → 38% is +7 percentage points (RD), but a 23% relative increase (RR).
- When the outcome is **common** (30-day mortality ≈ 33%), the OR is further from 1 than the RR and should not be read as a risk ratio.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**위험차** = 절대적 차이(%p), **위험비** = 상대적 차이, **오즈비** = 오즈의 비. 결과가 흔하면 오즈비는 위험비보다 1에서 더 멉니다.
:::

## Which measure when? · 어떤 척도를 쓸까?

| Measure | Use it when… | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **Risk difference** | You want the **clinical or public-health impact**: extra (or fewer) events per 100 patients. $1 / \text{RD}$ = number needed to treat (or harm) | RD 0.07 → 1 extra death per $1/0.07 ≈ 14$ patients treated |
| **Risk ratio** | You want the **relative strength** of an effect, or to compare groups with different baseline risks | "Risk of death was 23% higher with RHC" |
| **Odds ratio** | The model is **logistic regression**, or the design is **case-control** (risks cannot be estimated). Close to the RR only if the outcome is **rare** (< ~10%) | Comparing with Connors et al., who reported an OR |

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
Report an **absolute** (RD) and a **relative** (RR) measure together. Today: RD and RR, plus the OR to compare with Connors et al.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**위험차**: 임상적 영향(NNT). **위험비**: 상대적 크기. **오즈비**: 로지스틱 회귀, 환자-대조군 연구. 절대적·상대적 척도를 **함께** 보고하세요.
:::

## The workflow · 분석 흐름

```{r}
#| label: workflow
#| echo: false
#| out-width: 100%
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 2.7
wf <- tibble(
  x = 1:7,
  lab = c("0. Question\n(estimand)", "1. Covariates\n(pre-treatment\nonly)",
          "2. Estimate PS\n(logistic\nregression)", "3. Match\n(nearest\n+ caliper)",
          "4. Balance OK?\n(|SMD| < 0.1)", "5. Effect\n(outcome used\nonly here)",
          "6. Sensitivity\n(IPTW,\nE-value)"),
  col = c(rep("#bd93f9", 4), "#ffb86c", "#50fa7b", "#bd93f9"))
p_wf <- ggplot(wf) +
  geom_segment(data = wf[-7, ], aes(x = x + 0.42, xend = x + 0.58, y = 1, yend = 1),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm"), type = "closed"), colour = "#ff79c6", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_curve(aes(x = 5, y = 0.6, xend = 3, yend = 0.6), curvature = -0.35, colour = "#ffb86c",
             linetype = 2, arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm"))) +
  annotate("text", x = 4, y = 0.3, label = "balance not OK: revise the PS model",
           colour = "#ffb86c", size = 4) +
  geom_label(aes(x, 1, label = lab), fill = "#44475a", colour = "#f8f8f2", label.size = 0,
             size = 3.6, label.padding = unit(0.4, "lines"), lineheight = 0.95) +
  geom_point(aes(x, 1.38), colour = wf$col, size = 3) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0.5, 7.5), ylim = c(0.2, 1.45)) +
  theme_void() + theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#282a36", colour = NA))
attr(p_wf, "keep_theme") <- TRUE
p_wf
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- Steps **1–4 are the design stage**. Repeat them until balance is good — **without looking at the outcome**.
- Step **5** uses the outcome once. Step **6** checks how robust the answer is.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
1–4단계 = **설계 단계**: 결과(사망)를 보지 않고 균형이 좋아질 때까지 반복합니다. 결과는 5단계에서 **한 번만** 사용합니다.
:::

# Part 2 · Hands-on: the RHC study {background-color="#44475a"}

실습: 우심도자술(RHC) 자료

## Step 1 · Choose covariates · 공변량 선택

The starter script defines `covs`: the **50 baseline covariates** used by Connors et al.

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Include · 포함**

- Measured **before** treatment (day 1)
- Causes of the outcome and/or the treatment
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Exclude · 제외**

- Anything measured **after** treatment (discharge date, length of stay)
- The outcome itself
:::
::::

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (3 min)"}
1. How many covariates are in `covs`?
2. How many patients have a missing value in any of them? *(`complete.cases()`)*
3. Which variables in the whole data set have missing values? *(`is.na()`, `colSums()`)*
:::

```{r}
#| label: covs-check
#| output: false
length(covs)
sum(!complete.cases(rhc[, covs]))
miss <- colSums(is.na(rhc))
miss[miss > 0]
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**처치 이전**에 측정된 변수만 사용합니다. 처치 이후 변수를 넣으면 치료 효과의 일부를 지워버립니다.
:::

## Step 1 · Results · 결과

```{r}
#| label: covs-check-out
#| echo: false
length(covs)
sum(!complete.cases(rhc[, covs]))
miss[miss > 0]
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- **`r length(covs)`** covariates, with **`r sum(!complete.cases(rhc[, covs]))`** missing values → every patient can be used. Real EHR data are rarely this complete.
- Missing values occur only in variables we do **not** use: `cat2` (secondary diagnosis), `adld3p` (daily activities), `urin1` (urine output), `dschdte` (discharge date, measured after treatment), and `dthdte` (date of death — missing for survivors).
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
사용할 공변량에는 결측치가 없습니다. 실제 EHR 자료에서는 **결측치 처리**가 중요한 문제입니다.
:::

## Step 1 · Table 1 · 기초특성표

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (6 min)"}
Make a "Table 1" comparing RHC and non-RHC patients on these 10 covariates:

`age, sex, cat1, dnr1, ca, aps1, meanbp1, pafi1, hrt1, surv2md1`

1. Summarize by treatment group, with continuous variables as mean (SD). *(gtsummary: `tbl_summary()`)*
2. Add **p-values**, using a t-test for continuous variables and letting gtsummary choose the test for categorical ones. *(`add_p()`)*
3. Add the **standardized mean difference (SMD)**. *(`add_smd()` from the starter script)*
4. Save it as `tbl_before`.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="💡 Hint · 힌트"}
`add_p(test = all_continuous() ~ "t.test")`. For categorical variables gtsummary picks the chi-squared test, or **Fisher's exact test** when some categories are rare (as in `cat1`). With 5,735 patients Fisher's test runs out of memory unless it is **simulated**: add `test.args = all_tests("fisher.test") ~ list(simulate.p.value = TRUE)`.
:::

```{r}
#| label: table1
#| output: false
key_vars <- c("age", "sex", "cat1", "dnr1", "ca", "aps1", "meanbp1", "pafi1", "hrt1", "surv2md1")
var_labels <- list(age ~ "Age (years)", sex ~ "Sex", cat1 ~ "Primary diagnosis", dnr1 ~ "DNR order",
                   ca ~ "Cancer", aps1 ~ "APACHE III score", meanbp1 ~ "Mean blood pressure (mmHg)",
                   pafi1 ~ "PaO2/FiO2 ratio", hrt1 ~ "Heart rate (/min)",
                   surv2md1 ~ "Predicted 2-month survival")

tbl_before <- rhc |>
  select(swang1, all_of(key_vars)) |>
  tbl_summary(by = swang1, label = var_labels,
              statistic = all_continuous() ~ "{mean} ({sd})") |>
  add_p(test = all_continuous() ~ "t.test",
        test.args = all_tests("fisher.test") ~ list(simulate.p.value = TRUE)) |>
  add_smd() |>
  bold_labels()
tbl_before
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
두 군의 기초특성, **p-값**, **표준화 평균차이(SMD)**를 비교하는 표를 만드세요.
:::

## Step 1 · Table 1 · Results · 결과

```{r}
#| label: table1-out
#| echo: false
tbl_before
```

## Step 1 · Table 1 · Interpretation · 해석

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- Continuous variables are mean (SD); categorical variables are n (%).
- **SMD** = difference between groups in standard-deviation units (No RHC minus RHC). Look at its **absolute value**: above **0.1** means meaningful imbalance. For a categorical variable, one SMD summarizes all categories.
- RHC patients are clearly **sicker**:
  - APACHE III: `r round(mean(rhc$aps1[rhc$treat == 1]))` vs `r round(mean(rhc$aps1[rhc$treat == 0]))` (|SMD| = 0.50)
  - Mean blood pressure: `r round(mean(rhc$meanbp1[rhc$treat == 1]))` vs `r round(mean(rhc$meanbp1[rhc$treat == 0]))` mmHg; PaO₂/FiO₂ (oxygenation) is lower
  - Sepsis with organ failure (MOSF w/Sepsis): `r percent(mean(rhc$cat1[rhc$treat == 1] == "MOSF w/Sepsis"), 1)` vs `r percent(mean(rhc$cat1[rhc$treat == 0] == "MOSF w/Sepsis"), 1)`; DNR orders: `r percent(mean(rhc$dnr1[rhc$treat == 1] == "Yes"), 1)` vs `r percent(mean(rhc$dnr1[rhc$treat == 0] == "Yes"), 1)`
- One SMD per variable here (e.g., primary diagnosis 0.58 summarizes all 9 categories); later, cobalt shows one SMD **per category**.
- **p-values vs SMD:** age differs by only 1 year (|SMD| = 0.06, negligible), yet p = `r sprintf("%.3f", t.test(age ~ treat, data = rhc)$p.value)` — "significant" only because the sample is large. This is why we judge balance by the SMD.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
RHC 환자가 **더 위중**합니다. 나이는 차이가 1세에 불과하지만(SMD 0.06) p-값은 유의합니다 → 표본이 크면 작은 차이도 유의해지므로 균형은 **SMD**로 판단합니다.
:::

## Step 1 · The standardized mean difference · 표준화 평균차이

**Continuous variable** (pooled SD):
$$
\text{SMD} = \frac{\bar{x}_{\text{RHC}} - \bar{x}_{\text{no RHC}}}{\sqrt{(s_{\text{RHC}}^2 + s_{\text{no RHC}}^2)/2}}
$$

**Binary variable** with proportions $p_1$ (RHC) and $p_0$ (no RHC), since the variance of a 0/1 variable is $p(1-p)$:
$$
\text{SMD} = \frac{p_1 - p_0}{\sqrt{\big(p_1(1-p_1) + p_0(1-p_0)\big)/2}}
$$

- The difference in means in **standard-deviation units** → comparable across variables measured in different units. **|SMD| < 0.1** = good balance.
- **Why not p-values?** They depend on sample size: with 5,735 patients tiny differences are "significant" (like age in Table 1), and after matching real imbalance may look "non-significant".

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Check yourself · 확인 (2 min)"}
From Table 1: APACHE III is 61 (SD 20) with RHC and 51 (SD 19) without. Calculate the SMD by hand. Is it above 0.1?
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**SMD** = 평균(또는 비율) 차이를 표준편차로 나눈 값. **0.1 미만**이면 균형. p-값은 표본 크기에 따라 달라지므로 균형 판단에 쓰지 않습니다.
:::

## Step 1 · SMD for all 50 covariates · 모든 공변량

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (6 min)"}
1. Compute the SMD for **all** covariates in `covs`, with a 0.1 threshold. Save as `bal_before`. *(cobalt: `bal.tab()`)*
2. How many covariate terms are not balanced?
3. Plot the 15 largest |SMD| values as dots, with a line at 0.1. Save as `p_smd`.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="💡 Hint · 힌트"}
`bal.tab()` needs the covariates and the treatment vector. Use `binary = "std"` so binary variables also get an SMD. The SMDs are in `bal_before$Balance`.
:::

```{r}
#| label: smd-all
#| output: false
bal_before <- bal.tab(rhc[, covs], treat = rhc$treat,
                      binary = "std", s.d.denom = "pooled", thresholds = c(m = 0.1))
bal_before$Balanced.mean.diffs

p_smd <- bal_before$Balance |>
  rownames_to_column("covariate") |>
  slice_max(abs(Diff.Un), n = 15) |>
  ggplot(aes(abs(Diff.Un), reorder(covariate, abs(Diff.Un)))) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0.1, linetype = 2, colour = "orange") +
  geom_point(size = 3, colour = "#ff79c6") +
  labs(x = "|SMD| before matching", y = NULL, title = "15 most imbalanced covariates")
p_smd
```

## Step 1 · SMD · Results · 결과

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="38%"}
```{r}
#| label: smd-all-out
#| echo: false
bal_before$Balanced.mean.diffs
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- Each category of a factor counts separately: **`r nrow(bal_before$Balance)`** terms.
- **`r sum(bal_before$Balance$M.Threshold.Un == "Not Balanced, >0.1", na.rm = TRUE)`** have |SMD| > 0.1.
- The largest imbalances are all **severity markers**: APACHE III, blood pressure, oxygenation, sepsis.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="62%"}
```{r}
#| label: smd-plot-out
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 4.0
p_smd
```
:::
::::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
매칭 전 `r nrow(bal_before$Balance)`개 항목 중 `r sum(bal_before$Balance$M.Threshold.Un == "Not Balanced, >0.1", na.rm = TRUE)`개가 불균형이며, 대부분 **중증도** 관련 변수입니다.
:::

## Two tools for every effect estimate · 효과 추정 도구

From here on, every effect is estimated the same way: **fit a model (`lm()` or `glm()`), then call `avg_comparisons()`** (package **marginaleffects**).

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**What `avg_comparisons()` does · 하는 일**

1. Predict each patient's risk **as if treated** (`treat = 1`)
2. Predict again **as if untreated** (`treat = 0`)
3. **Average** each over the chosen patients (all → ATE; treated → ATT, via `newdata`)
4. **Compare** the averages: RD (default), RR, or OR (`comparison`)

…and computes the **standard error** you choose (`vcov`).
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Why robust standard errors? · 강건 표준오차**

- Ordinary SEs assume equal variance for everyone. For a 0/1 outcome the variance is $p(1-p)$ and differs between groups → ordinary SEs are wrong.
- **Robust ("sandwich") SEs**, `vcov = "HC3"`, fix this. HC3 adds a small-sample correction and is the default in the **sandwich** package; with 5,735 patients all robust versions agree.
- **Cluster-robust SEs**, `vcov = ~subclass`, also account for matched pairs (Step 5).
:::
::::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**`avg_comparisons()`**: 각 환자의 위험을 치료한 경우와 치료하지 않은 경우로 예측해 평균을 비교합니다. **강건 표준오차**: 0/1 결과에서는 분산이 군마다 다르므로 사용합니다.
:::

## The crude comparison · 단순 비교

What would we conclude if we ignored confounding?

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (5 min)"}
1. Compute the number of patients, deaths, and 30-day risk of death in each group.
2. Estimate the **crude risk difference** with a 95% CI, using a linear model of `died30` on `treat` and robust standard errors. Save as `crude`.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="💡 Hint · 힌트"}
`avg_comparisons()` (marginaleffects) gives the risk difference for `treat`. Use `vcov = "HC3"` for robust standard errors.
:::

```{r}
#| label: crude
#| output: false
crude_tab <- rhc |>
  group_by(swang1) |>
  summarise(n = n(), deaths = sum(died30), risk30 = mean(died30))
crude_tab

crude_fit <- lm(died30 ~ treat, data = rhc)
crude <- avg_comparisons(crude_fit, variables = "treat", vcov = "HC3")
crude
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
교란을 무시한 **단순 비교**입니다. 나중에 보정한 결과와 비교할 기준이 됩니다.
:::

## The crude comparison · Results · 결과

```{r}
#| label: crude-out
#| echo: false
crude_tab
crude
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- 30-day mortality was **`r percent(crude_tab$risk30[2], 0.1)`** with RHC and **`r percent(crude_tab$risk30[1], 0.1)`** without.
- Reading the `avg_comparisons()` output:
  - `Estimate` = risk difference = **`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * crude$estimate)` percentage points**
  - `2.5 %` to `97.5 %` = 95% CI: **`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * crude$conf.low)` to `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * crude$conf.high)`** points
  - `Pr(>|z|)` = p-value. `S` = $-\log_2(p)$, evidence against "no difference" in bits: as surprising as `S` heads in a row from a fair coin (p = 0.05 ≈ 4 heads)
- This is an **association**: RHC patients were much sicker, so part of this difference is confounding.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
단순 비교: RHC군의 30일 사망 위험이 `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * crude$estimate)`%p 높습니다. 그러나 **중증도의 영향이 섞여** 있습니다.
:::

## Step 2 · Estimate the propensity score · 성향점수 추정

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (6 min)"}
1. Fit a **logistic regression** of `treat` on all 50 covariates. Save as `ps_model`. *(`glm()`; `reformulate()` builds a formula from `covs`)*
2. Save each patient's predicted probability of RHC as a new column `ps`. *(`predict()`)*
3. Summarize the PS (mean, median, min, max) by treatment group.
4. Now let **MatchIt** estimate the same PS, without matching yet: `matchit()` with `method = NULL` and `distance = "glm"`. The PS is stored in `$distance`. Is it identical to yours?
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="💡 Hint · 힌트"}
`predict()` returns log-odds unless you ask for `type = "response"`.
:::

```{r}
#| label: ps-model
#| output: false
ps_formula <- reformulate(covs, response = "treat")
ps_model   <- glm(ps_formula, family = binomial, data = rhc)
rhc$ps     <- predict(ps_model, type = "response")

ps_summary <- rhc |>
  group_by(swang1) |>
  summarise(mean_ps = mean(ps), median_ps = median(ps), min_ps = min(ps), max_ps = max(ps))
ps_summary

# Same PS from MatchIt (no matching yet)
m0 <- matchit(ps_formula, data = rhc, method = NULL, distance = "glm")
max(abs(m0$distance - rhc$ps))      # difference between the two: essentially 0
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
성향점수 모형 = **치료 여부**를 종속변수로 하는 로지스틱 회귀. `glm()`으로 직접 추정하거나, **MatchIt**이 내부에서 같은 `glm()`으로 추정합니다.
:::

## Step 2 · Results · 결과

```{r}
#| label: ps-model-out
#| echo: false
ps_summary
max(abs(m0$distance - rhc$ps))
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- Each patient now has a PS: the estimated probability of receiving RHC given their 50 covariates.
- The average PS is **`r sprintf("%.2f", ps_summary$mean_ps[2])`** for RHC patients and **`r sprintf("%.2f", ps_summary$mean_ps[1])`** for non-RHC patients: the model separates the groups, as expected. The ranges overlap widely, so comparable patients exist in both groups.
- The largest difference between your `glm()` PS and MatchIt's PS is essentially **0**: `matchit()` fits the same logistic regression internally. In practice you can let MatchIt do it; **cobalt** then checks balance but does not estimate the PS.
- The PS model's **only job is to create balance**. Do not interpret its coefficients as causal, and do not drop "non-significant" variables.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
`glm()`과 MatchIt의 성향점수는 **동일**합니다. 성향점수 모형의 목표는 예측 정확도가 아니라 **공변량 균형**입니다.
:::

## Step 2 · Who gets RHC? · 어떤 환자가 RHC를 받나?

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (4 min)"}
1. Turn `ps_model` into a table of **odds ratios** with 95% CIs. *(broom: `tidy()`)*
2. Drop the intercept and keep the **8 strongest** predictors (largest |z| statistic). Save as `ps_or`.
3. Discuss: do these make clinical sense?
:::

```{r}
#| label: ps-or
#| output: false
ps_or <- tidy(ps_model, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) |>
  filter(term != "(Intercept)") |>
  slice_max(abs(statistic), n = 8) |>
  select(term, OR = estimate, conf.low, conf.high, p.value)
ps_or
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
성향점수 모형의 오즈비로 **어떤 환자가 RHC를 받았는지** 살펴봅니다.
:::

## Step 2 · Who gets RHC? · Results · 결과

```{r}
#| label: ps-or-out
#| echo: false
ps_or |>
  gt() |> fmt_number(c(OR, conf.low, conf.high), decimals = 3) |>
  fmt_scientific(p.value, decimals = 1) |>
  tab_header("Strongest predictors of receiving RHC")
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- OR > 1 → more likely to receive RHC; OR < 1 → less likely.
- Continuous variables are **per 1 unit**, so their ORs are close to 1. For PaO₂/FiO₂ (OR 0.995), a value 100 units lower raises the odds of RHC about **1.6-fold**.
- **More RHC:** worse oxygenation, lower blood pressure, cardiovascular diagnosis (`cardYes`, OR 1.75), sepsis with organ failure (OR 1.71).
- **Less RHC:** a DNR order (OR 0.51).
- Clinically sensible: RHC went to **unstable** patients receiving full treatment.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
산소화가 나쁘고 혈압이 낮은 **불안정한 환자**가 RHC를 더 많이 받았고, DNR 환자는 덜 받았습니다.
:::

## Step 2 · Check overlap · 중첩 확인

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (4 min)"}
1. Plot the **distribution of the PS** for each treatment group in one graph. Save as `p_overlap`. *(`geom_density()`)*
2. How many RHC and non-RHC patients have a PS above 0.9?
:::

```{r}
#| label: ps-overlap
#| output: false
high_ps <- count(rhc, swang1, ps > 0.9)
high_ps

p_overlap <- ggplot(rhc, aes(x = ps, fill = swang1)) +
  geom_density(alpha = 0.5, colour = NA) +
  labs(x = "Propensity score", y = "Density", fill = NULL,
       title = "Propensity score distribution by group")
p_overlap
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
두 군의 성향점수 분포가 **겹쳐야(overlap)** 비교가 가능합니다.
:::

## Step 2 · Overlap · Results · 결과

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="60%"}
```{r}
#| label: ps-overlap-out
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 3.2
p_overlap
```
:::
::: {.column width="40%"}
```{r}
#| label: ps-high-out
#| echo: false
high_ps
```
:::
::::

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- RHC patients (pink) have **higher** propensity scores, as expected.
- The curves **overlap** over most of the range, so matching is feasible.
- Above PS 0.9 there are **`r high_ps$n[high_ps$swang1 == "RHC" & high_ps[["ps > 0.9"]]]`** RHC patients but only **`r high_ps$n[high_ps$swang1 == "No RHC" & high_ps[["ps > 0.9"]]]`** controls: the patients **most strongly predicted to receive RHC** have few comparable controls, so some will go unmatched (a **positivity** problem). Who these patients are, we check in Step 3.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
RHC를 받을 가능성이 **가장 높은** 환자들은 비교할 대조군이 거의 없습니다 → **양수성** 문제. 이들이 어떤 환자인지는 3단계에서 확인합니다.
:::

## How nearest-neighbour matching works · 최근접 이웃 매칭의 원리

A toy example of **1:1** nearest-neighbour matching (one control per RHC patient): 5 RHC patients and 8 controls, placed by their **logit PS**. Caliper = 0.3.

```{r}
#| label: nn-toy
#| echo: false
#| out-width: 100%
#| fig-width: 11
#| fig-height: 2.9
tr <- tibble(id = paste0("T", 1:5), x = c(-1.0, 0.2, 0.9, 1.5, 3.2))
co <- tibble(id = paste0("C", 1:8), x = c(-1.3, -0.9, -0.2, 0.1, 0.35, 1.0, 1.7, 2.1))
pairs <- tibble(t = c(-1.0, 0.2, 0.9, 1.5), c = c(-0.9, 0.1, 1.0, 1.7))
used <- co$x %in% pairs$c
p_nn <- ggplot() +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 3.2 - 0.3, xmax = 3.2 + 0.3, ymin = -0.25, ymax = 1.25,
           fill = "#ffb86c", alpha = 0.15) +
  annotate("text", x = 3.2, y = -0.45, label = "caliper: no control within 0.3", colour = "#ffb86c", size = 3.8) +
  geom_segment(data = pairs, aes(x = t, xend = c, y = 1, yend = 0), colour = "#50fa7b", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_point(data = tr, aes(x, 1), colour = "#ff79c6", size = 6) +
  geom_point(data = co, aes(x, 0), colour = ifelse(used, "#8be9fd", "#6272a4"), size = 6) +
  geom_text(data = tr, aes(x, 1, label = id), colour = "#282a36", size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
  geom_text(data = co, aes(x, 0, label = id), colour = "#282a36", size = 3, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("text", x = -1.9, y = c(1, 0), label = c("RHC", "No RHC"), colour = c("#ff79c6", "#8be9fd"),
           size = 4.5, hjust = 1, fontface = "bold") +
  annotate("segment", x = -1.5, xend = 3.6, y = -0.75, yend = -0.75, colour = "#f8f8f2",
           arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.2, "cm"))) +
  annotate("text", x = 1, y = -0.95, label = "logit(PS): higher = more likely to receive RHC", colour = "#f8f8f2", size = 3.8) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-2.6, 3.7), ylim = c(-1.05, 1.3)) +
  theme_void() + theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#282a36", colour = NA))
attr(p_nn, "keep_theme") <- TRUE
p_nn
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
1. MatchIt starts with the RHC patient that is **hardest to match** (highest PS, T5) and works down.
2. Each RHC patient is paired with the control whose PS is **closest** (green lines) — the **nearest neighbour**.
3. **1:1 without replacement:** each RHC patient gets **one** control, and a used control leaves the pool.
4. If no control lies within the **caliper**, the RHC patient stays **unmatched** (T5). Unused controls (grey: C1, C3, C5, C8) are dropped.

With `ratio = 2`, MatchIt repeats steps 1–3 to give each RHC patient a **second** control.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**1:1 최근접 이웃 매칭**: 각 RHC 환자에게 성향점수가 가장 가까운 대조군 **한 명**을 짝지어 줍니다. 사용된 대조군은 다시 쓰지 않으며(비복원), 캘리퍼 안에 대조군이 없으면 제외됩니다.
:::

## Step 3 · Match · 매칭

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (5 min)"}
Match RHC patients to non-RHC patients with **`matchit()`** (MatchIt) using this design. Save as `m_out`, then look at how many patients were matched. *(`summary()`)*

| Design choice | Setting | Argument |
|---|---|---|
| Matching method | nearest neighbour (closest PS first) | `method` |
| Controls per RHC patient | **1** (1:1) | `ratio` |
| Reuse of controls | **no** — each control used once (without replacement) | `replace` |
| Distance | PS from logistic regression, on the **logit** scale | `distance`, `link` |
| Caliper | **0.2** standard deviations of the logit PS | `caliper` |
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="💡 Hint · 힌트"}
All arguments are described in `?matchit`; `link = "linear.logit"` gives the logit scale.
:::

```{r}
#| label: match
#| output: false
m_out <- matchit(ps_formula, data = rhc,
                 method = "nearest", distance = "glm", link = "linear.logit",
                 caliper = 0.2, ratio = 1, replace = FALSE)
m_out
summary(m_out)$nn
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**최근접 이웃 1:1 매칭**: 각 RHC 환자에게 성향점수가 가장 가까운 비RHC 환자 한 명을 짝지어 줍니다. **캘리퍼** = 허용되는 최대 거리.
:::

## Step 3 · Match · Results · 결과

```{r}
#| label: match-out
#| echo: false
summary(m_out)$nn
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- `All`: before matching, `r summary(m_out)$nn["All", "Treated"]` RHC and `r summary(m_out)$nn["All", "Control"]` non-RHC patients.
- `Matched`: **`r summary(m_out)$nn["Matched", "Treated"]` pairs**.
- `Unmatched`: **`r summary(m_out)$nn["Unmatched", "Treated"]` RHC patients** had no control within the caliper (`r sprintf("%.2f", m_out$caliper)` on the logit scale) and were dropped; `r summary(m_out)$nn["Unmatched", "Control"]` controls were not needed.
- `ESS` (effective sample size, $(\sum w)^2 / \sum w^2$) equals the matched number here, because in 1:1 matching every matched patient has weight 1.
- Printing `m_out` also shows the **target estimand: ATT**.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
`r summary(m_out)$nn["Matched", "Treated"]`쌍이 매칭되었고, RHC 환자 `r summary(m_out)$nn["Unmatched", "Treated"]`명은 캘리퍼 안에 대조군이 없어 제외되었습니다.
:::

## Step 3 · What do matched pairs look like? · 매칭된 쌍의 예

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (4 min)"}
Extract the matched data (`match.data(m_out)`, save as `md`). Each pair shares a `subclass` number. Look at pairs **1, 1351, and 664**: how close are their PS values? How close are their other covariates?
:::

```{r}
#| label: pairs
#| output: false
md <- match.data(m_out)
md |>
  filter(subclass %in% c(1, 1351, 664)) |>     # one low-, one middle-, one high-PS pair
  arrange(ps) |>
  select(subclass, swang1, ps, age, cat1, aps1, meanbp1, pafi1)
```

```{r}
#| label: pairs-out
#| echo: false
pick <- c(1, 1351, 664)
md |>
  filter(subclass %in% pick) |>
  arrange(ps) |> arrange(match(subclass, pick), desc(treat)) |>
  transmute(Pair = as.character(subclass), Group = as.character(swang1), PS = ps,
            Age = round(age), Diagnosis = as.character(cat1), `APACHE III` = aps1,
            `Mean BP` = meanbp1, `PaO2/FiO2` = round(pafi1)) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(PS, decimals = 3) |>
  tab_style(style = cell_text(color = "#50fa7b", weight = "bold"), locations = cells_body(columns = PS))
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- `subclass` is just a pair ID; these three were chosen because their PS is low, middle, and high. Within each pair the **PS is very close** (green) — always within the caliper.
- Other covariates can still **differ** — different age, diagnosis, or severity. Matched patients are **not twins**.
- That is fine: balance holds at the **group** level. Across all `r nrow(md) / 2` pairs the differences cancel out, as the balance checks in Step 4 show.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
쌍 안에서 성향점수는 매우 가깝지만 다른 변수는 다를 수 있습니다. 균형은 **개인**이 아니라 **집단** 수준에서 이루어집니다.
:::

## Step 3 · Who was left out? · 누가 제외되었나?

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (5 min)"}
1. Among RHC patients, compare the **matched** and **unmatched** ones: number, mean PS, mean APACHE III. *(matched patients have a weight > 0 in `m_out$weights`)*
2. Plot the PS distributions before and after matching as **mirrored histograms**. Save as `p_mirror`. *(cobalt: `bal.plot()`)*
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="💡 Hint · 힌트"}
In `bal.plot()`, the PS is called `"distance"`; ask for both samples and a mirrored histogram (see `?bal.plot`).
:::

```{r}
#| label: unmatched
#| output: false
md <- match.data(m_out)

unmatched_tab <- rhc |>
  mutate(matched = m_out$weights > 0) |>
  filter(treat == 1) |>
  group_by(matched) |>
  summarise(n = n(), mean_ps = mean(ps), mean_aps = mean(aps1))
unmatched_tab

p_mirror <- bal.plot(m_out, var.name = "distance", which = "both",
                     type = "histogram", mirror = TRUE,
                     sample.names = c("Before matching", "After matching"))
p_mirror
```

## Step 3 · Who was left out? · Results · 결과

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
```{r}
#| label: mirror-out
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6
#| fig-height: 3.2
p_mirror
```
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
```{r}
#| label: unmatched-out
#| echo: false
unmatched_tab
```
:::
::::

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- **Histograms:** controls on top (red), RHC patients below (teal). Before matching the shapes differ; after matching they are near **mirror images**.
- **Table:** the `r unmatched_tab$n[!unmatched_tab$matched]` unmatched RHC patients had a much higher PS (`r sprintf("%.2f", unmatched_tab$mean_ps[!unmatched_tab$matched])` vs `r sprintf("%.2f", unmatched_tab$mean_ps[unmatched_tab$matched])`) and, **on average**, higher APACHE III (`r round(unmatched_tab$mean_aps[!unmatched_tab$matched])` vs `r round(unmatched_tab$mean_aps[unmatched_tab$matched])`): they were **sicker** and almost always received RHC in practice.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
제외된 RHC 환자는 RHC를 받을 가능성이 가장 높았고, **평균적으로 더 위중**했습니다.
:::

## Step 3 · Why the left-out patients matter · 제외된 환자의 의미

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- **The estimand changes.** We aimed for the ATT (all RHC patients), but estimate the effect in **RHC patients who could be matched**: `r summary(m_out)$nn["Matched", "Treated"]` of `r sum(rhc$treat)`.
- **We learn nothing about the excluded group** — arguably the patients RHC was meant for. If RHC is more harmful in them, the true ATT is larger; if it helps them, smaller. The data cannot tell us.
- **It is a positivity problem, not just a statistical step:** almost every patient this sick got RHC, so there is little information on what would have happened without it.
- **What to do:** report how many were excluded and how they differ; state the population the result applies to; compare with a method that keeps everyone (full matching, weighting).
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
결과는 **매칭 가능한** RHC 환자에게만 적용됩니다. 제외된 환자에서의 효과는 알 수 없으므로 제외된 수와 특성을 보고하고, 모든 환자를 사용하는 방법과 비교하세요.
:::

## Step 4 · Check balance · 균형 진단

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (4 min)"}
1. Compute the SMDs **before and after** matching for all covariates, with a 0.1 threshold. Save as `bal_after`. *(`bal.tab()` on `m_out`)*
2. How many covariate terms are balanced after matching?
3. What is the largest |SMD| after matching?
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="💡 Hint · 힌트"}
By default `bal.tab()` shows only the **after**-matching SMDs. Add `un = TRUE` to also see the **before**-matching values (columns ending in `.Un`). This option is documented in `?display-options`, not in `?bal.tab`.
:::

```{r}
#| label: baltab
#| output: false
bal_after <- bal.tab(m_out, un = TRUE, binary = "std", thresholds = c(m = 0.1))
bal_after$Balanced.mean.diffs
max(abs(bal_after$Balance$Diff.Adj[-1]))   # row 1 is the PS itself
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
매칭 후 **모든** 공변량의 |SMD|가 0.1 미만인지 확인합니다. 아직 결과(사망)는 보지 않습니다!
:::

## Step 4 · Balance · Results · 결과

```{r}
#| label: baltab-out
#| echo: false
bal_after$Balanced.mean.diffs
max(abs(bal_after$Balance$Diff.Adj[-1]))
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- Before matching, `r sum(bal_before$Balance$M.Threshold.Un == "Not Balanced, >0.1", na.rm = TRUE)` of `r nrow(bal_before$Balance)` covariate terms were imbalanced (Step 1).
- After matching, **all `r sum(bal_after$Balance$M.Threshold == "Balanced, <0.1", na.rm = TRUE)`** are balanced; the largest |SMD| is **`r sprintf("%.3f", max(abs(bal_after$Balance$Diff.Adj[-1])))`**.
- If balance were poor, we would return to Step 2 (e.g., add splines or interactions to the PS model) — still without looking at the outcome.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
매칭 후 모든 항목의 |SMD| < 0.1 → **측정된** 공변량의 균형이 확보되었습니다.
:::

## Step 4 · Table 1 before and after · 매칭 전후 비교표

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (5 min)"}
1. Make the same table as `tbl_before` (with p-values and SMD), but using the matched data `md`. Save as `tbl_after`.
2. Combine the two tables side by side. Save as `tbl_merged`. *(gtsummary: `tbl_merge()`)*
:::

```{r}
#| label: table1-after
#| output: false
tbl_after <- md |>
  select(swang1, all_of(key_vars)) |>
  tbl_summary(by = swang1, label = var_labels,
              statistic = all_continuous() ~ "{mean} ({sd})") |>
  add_p(test = all_continuous() ~ "t.test",
        test.args = all_tests("fisher.test") ~ list(simulate.p.value = TRUE)) |>
  add_smd() |>
  bold_labels()

tbl_merged <- tbl_merge(list(tbl_before, tbl_after),
                        tab_spanner = c("**Before matching**", "**After matching**"))
tbl_merged
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
논문에서는 **매칭 전후 기초특성표**를 나란히 보여줍니다.
:::

## Step 4 · Table 1 before and after · Results · 결과

```{r}
#| label: table1-after-out
#| echo: false
tbl_merged
```

## Step 4 · Table 1 before and after · Interpretation · 해석

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- **Left:** the original groups (`r sum(rhc$treat == 0)` vs `r sum(rhc$treat == 1)`). **Right:** the matched groups (`r nrow(md) / 2` vs `r nrow(md) / 2`).
- After matching, the groups look alike:
  - APACHE III: `r round(mean(md$aps1[md$treat == 1]))` vs `r round(mean(md$aps1[md$treat == 0]))`; sepsis with organ failure: `r percent(mean(md$cat1[md$treat == 1] == "MOSF w/Sepsis"), 1)` vs `r percent(mean(md$cat1[md$treat == 0] == "MOSF w/Sepsis"), 1)`
  - Every |SMD| is now below 0.1
- **p-values:** most are now large, partly just because the sample is smaller. Yet APACHE III (p = `r sprintf("%.3f", t.test(aps1 ~ treat, data = md)$p.value)`) and PaO₂/FiO₂ (p = `r sprintf("%.3f", t.test(pafi1 ~ treat, data = md)$p.value)`) are still "significant" although their |SMD| is below 0.1. P-values are not a measure of balance; the SMD is.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
매칭 후 모든 |SMD| < 0.1입니다. 일부 p-값은 여전히 유의하지만 이는 균형의 척도가 아닙니다. 균형은 **SMD**로 판단합니다.
:::

## Step 4 · The cost of matching · 매칭의 대가

We used **`r nrow(md)` of `r format(nrow(rhc), big.mark = ",")`** patients. Who was lost, and why does it matter?

| Lost | Number | Implication |
|---|---|---|
| RHC patients with no comparable control | **`r summary(m_out)$nn["Unmatched", "Treated"]`** (`r percent(summary(m_out)$nn["Unmatched", "Treated"] / sum(rhc$treat), 1)` of RHC patients) | Those most strongly predicted to receive RHC, and **on average the sickest**. Our result does **not** apply to them: the estimand shifts from "all RHC patients" to "RHC patients who could be matched" |
| Controls not needed | **`r summary(m_out)$nn["Unmatched", "Control"]`** | Their information is unused → **wider confidence intervals** (less precision) |

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- **Generalizability:** if RHC works differently in these patients (more harm, or perhaps benefit), our estimate cannot show it. Report who was excluded.
- **Precision:** fewer patients → more uncertainty.
- **Alternatives that keep more patients:** matching with replacement, full matching, or weighting (IPTW, overlap weights). We try some of these next.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
RHC를 받을 가능성이 가장 높았고 평균적으로 더 위중한 RHC 환자 `r summary(m_out)$nn["Unmatched", "Treated"]`명이 제외되어 결과를 이들에게 **일반화할 수 없고**, 사용하지 않은 대조군 때문에 **정밀도**가 낮아집니다.
:::

## Step 4 · The Love plot · 러브 플롯

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (3 min)"}
Draw a **Love plot**: the absolute SMD of every covariate before and after matching, with a line at 0.1, sorted by the imbalance before matching. Save as `p_love`. *(cobalt: `love.plot()`)*
:::

```{r}
#| label: loveplot
#| output: false
p_love <- love.plot(m_out, binary = "std", abs = TRUE,
                    thresholds = c(m = 0.1), var.order = "unadjusted",
                    drop.distance = TRUE,
                    colors = c("#ff5555", "#50fa7b"), shapes = c(16, 17),
                    sample.names = c("Before", "After"))
p_love
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**러브 플롯**: 모든 공변량의 매칭 전후 SMD를 한 그림에 보여줍니다.
:::

- Each row is one covariate term, sorted by imbalance before matching. To keep labels readable, the slide shows the **25 most imbalanced** of the 70 terms; your own plot shows all of them.
- x-axis: |SMD|. Dashed line: 0.1.
- **Red circles (before):** many far to the right (up to about 0.55).
- **Green triangles (after):** all to the **left** of 0.1.

매칭 후(초록) 모든 점이 0.1 선 **왼쪽**에 있습니다 → 균형 확보.
