## Step 4 · Beyond the mean · 분포 전체 확인

Equal means do not guarantee equal distributions.

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (4 min)"}
1. Get the **variance ratios** (variance in RHC ÷ variance in controls) for `aps1`, `pafi1`, and `meanbp1`, before and after matching. *(`bal.tab()`; see its `stats` argument)*
2. Plot the full distribution of `aps1` and of `pafi1` before and after matching. Show the two plots side by side. *(`bal.plot()`, patchwork)*
:::

```{r}
#| label: balplot-vars
#| output: false
vr_tab <- bal.tab(m_out, stats = c("m", "v"), un = TRUE)$Balance[
  c("aps1", "pafi1", "meanbp1"), c("Diff.Un", "Diff.Adj", "V.Ratio.Un", "V.Ratio.Adj")]
vr_tab

p_aps  <- bal.plot(m_out, var.name = "aps1",  which = "both",
                   sample.names = c("Before", "After")) + labs(title = "APACHE III (aps1)")
p_pafi <- bal.plot(m_out, var.name = "pafi1", which = "both",
                   sample.names = c("Before", "After")) + labs(title = "PaO2/FiO2 (pafi1)")
p_aps + p_pafi
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
평균뿐 아니라 **분포 전체**와 **분산비**도 확인합니다.
:::

## Step 4 · Beyond the mean · Results · 결과

```{r}
#| label: balplot-out
#| echo: false
#| layout-ncol: 2
#| fig-width: 5.5
#| fig-height: 2.3
p_aps
p_pafi
```

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
```{r}
#| label: vr-out
#| echo: false
round(vr_tab, 2)
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
매칭 후 분포가 겹치고 분산비가 1에 가깝습니다 → **분포 전체**가 비슷해졌습니다. PaO₂/FiO₂ 333 부근의 봉우리는 검사를 하지 않아 **정상값으로 채운 값**(결측)입니다.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- **Plots** (red = no RHC, teal = RHC): RHC patients have higher APACHE III and lower PaO₂/FiO₂ before matching; after, the curves **overlap**.
- **Table:** `Diff` = SMD, `V.Ratio` = variance ratio, before (`.Un`) and after (`.Adj`). A ratio near **1** (acceptable 0.5–2) means similar spread; after matching all are close to 1.
- **Spike in PaO₂/FiO₂ (~333):** a "normal" value filled in when no blood gas was measured, so it marks **missing information**, not real oxygenation. In EHR data, whether a test was done can itself be informative.
:::
:::
::::

## Step 4 · Try other matching settings · 매칭 옵션 실험

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (10 min)"}
Re-run the matching, changing **one** setting at a time:

1. caliper **0.2** (our choice)
2. caliper **0.05**
3. **no** caliper
4. **2** controls per RHC patient, **with** replacement
5. **full** matching (`method = "full"`)

For each, record in your script: (a) the number of matched RHC patients and (b) the largest |SMD| after matching. Which setting would you choose, and why?
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="💡 Hint · 힌트"}
Writing a small function that runs `matchit()` with given settings and returns (a) and (b) saves a lot of copying.
:::

```{r}
#| label: experiment
#| output: false
fit_variant <- function(...) {
  m <- matchit(ps_formula, data = rhc, link = "linear.logit", ...)
  tibble(matched_treated = summary(m)$nn["Matched", "Treated"],
         matched_controls = round(summary(m)$nn["Matched", "Control"]),
         max_abs_smd = max(abs(bal.tab(m, binary = "std")$Balance$Diff.Adj[-1])))
}
exp_res <- bind_rows(
  "caliper 0.2"          = fit_variant(method = "nearest", caliper = 0.2),
  "caliper 0.05"         = fit_variant(method = "nearest", caliper = 0.05),
  "no caliper"           = fit_variant(method = "nearest"),
  "2:1 with replacement" = fit_variant(method = "nearest", caliper = 0.2, ratio = 2, replace = TRUE),
  "full matching"        = fit_variant(method = "full"),
  .id = "setting")
exp_res
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
매칭 설정을 하나씩 바꾸며 **매칭된 환자 수**와 **최대 |SMD|**를 비교하세요.
:::

## Step 4 · Matching settings · Results · 결과

```{r}
#| label: experiment-out
#| echo: false
exp_res |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(max_abs_smd, decimals = 3) |>
  cols_label(setting = "Setting", matched_treated = "Matched RHC patients",
             matched_controls = "Controls used", max_abs_smd = "Largest |SMD|")
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- **Caliper 0.05:** fewer RHC patients matched, better balance.
- **No caliper:** all RHC patients matched, but poor pairs are kept → balance **fails** (largest |SMD| > 0.1).
- **2:1 with replacement:** more controls per RHC patient; controls can be reused (some count more than once).
- **Full matching:** keeps **everyone** by forming weighted groups, with good balance.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
캘리퍼를 좁히면 균형은 좋아지지만 매칭되는 환자 수가 줄어듭니다.
:::

## The bias–variance trade-off · 편향–분산 상충관계

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Bias · 편향** = **systematic** error

- From comparing patients who are **not truly comparable** (poor matches → leftover confounding)
- Does not shrink with a larger sample
- Reduced by **tighter** matching
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Variance · 분산** = **random** error

- From having **few patients** → wide confidence intervals
- Reduced by **keeping more** patients (looser caliper, more controls, full matching, weighting)
:::
::::

| Choice | Bias | Variance |
|---|---|---|
| Tight caliper (0.05) | lower (only close matches) | higher (fewer patients) |
| No caliper | higher (poor pairs kept) | lower (all RHC patients kept) |
| Full matching / weighting | low **if** balance is good **and** overlap is adequate | depends on the weights: low if similar, **high if some are extreme** (check ESS) |

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
No method is always best. Keeping everyone avoids discarding patients, but unequal weights lower the ESS. Aim for **good balance (|SMD| < 0.1)**, adequate **ESS**, and acceptable **overlap**, and choose the setting **before** looking at the outcome.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**편향** = 비교 불가능한 환자를 비교해 생기는 체계적 오차. **분산** = 환자 수가 적어 생기는 무작위 오차. 엄격한 매칭: 편향↓ 분산↑. 결과를 보기 **전에** 설정을 정하세요.
:::

## Step 5 · Risk difference · 위험차 추정

Only now do we look at the outcome · 이제서야 결과(사망)를 봅니다.

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (6 min)"}
1. In the matched data `md`, fit a linear model of `died30` on `treat`, using the matching `weights`.
2. Estimate the **ATT risk difference** with a 95% CI. Save as `att_rd`. *(`avg_comparisons()`)*
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="💡 Hint · 힌트"}
- Matched pairs are not independent: use cluster-robust standard errors by pair, `vcov = ~subclass`.
- To average over the **treated** patients (ATT), add `newdata = subset(md, treat == 1)`.
- In 1:1 matching every `weights` value is 1, so it changes nothing here. Keep it: with other matching methods the weights differ and are required.
:::

```{r}
#| label: effect
#| output: false
fit <- lm(died30 ~ treat, data = md, weights = weights)
att_rd <- avg_comparisons(fit, variables = "treat",
                          vcov = ~subclass,
                          newdata = subset(md, treat == 1))
att_rd
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
매칭된 쌍을 군집으로 보는 **군집-강건 표준오차**로 **위험차**를 추정합니다.
:::

## Step 5 · Risk difference · Results · 결과

```{r}
#| label: effect-out
#| echo: false
att_rd
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- **ATT risk difference = `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * att_rd$estimate)` percentage points** (95% CI `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * att_rd$conf.low)` to `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * att_rd$conf.high)`; p `r ifelse(att_rd$p.value < 0.001, "< 0.001", sprintf("= %.3f", att_rd$p.value))`).
- Among matched RHC patients there were about **`r round(100 * att_rd$estimate)` more deaths per 100 patients** (95% CI `r round(100 * att_rd$conf.low)` to `r round(100 * att_rd$conf.high)`) within 30 days than among similar patients without RHC.
- Smaller than the crude difference (`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * crude$estimate)` points): part of the crude difference was confounding — but not all of it.
- **Where is the propensity score?** The model is a simple comparison of death rates. The PS did its work earlier, by choosing the patients in `md`. The same model on the full data `rhc` gives the crude estimate.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**ATT 위험차** = `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * att_rd$estimate)`%p: 매칭된 RHC 환자에서 100명당 약 `r round(100 * att_rd$estimate)`명 더 사망했습니다 (95% CI `r round(100 * att_rd$conf.low)`–`r round(100 * att_rd$conf.high)`명) — 비슷한 비시행 환자와 비교한 결과입니다. 성향점수는 결과 모형이 아니라 **분석할 환자를 선택**하는 데 사용되었습니다.
:::

## Step 5 · Risk ratio and odds ratio · 위험비와 오즈비

One model, three effect measures: only the `comparison` argument changes.

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (5 min)"}
Using the **same model** `fit` from the risk-difference step:

1. Estimate the **ATT risk ratio** with a 95% CI. Save as `att_rr`.
2. Estimate the **ATT odds ratio** with a 95% CI, to compare with Connors et al. Save as `att_or`.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="💡 Hint · 힌트"}
In `avg_comparisons()`, add `comparison = "lnratioavg"` (risk ratio) or `comparison = "lnoravg"` (odds ratio), with `transform = "exp"`. `ln` = computed on the log scale; `avg` = ratio of the **average** risks.
:::

```{r}
#| label: effect-rr
#| output: false
att_rr <- avg_comparisons(fit, variables = "treat", vcov = ~subclass,
                          newdata = subset(md, treat == 1),
                          comparison = "lnratioavg", transform = "exp")
att_or <- avg_comparisons(fit, variables = "treat", vcov = ~subclass,
                          newdata = subset(md, treat == 1),
                          comparison = "lnoravg", transform = "exp")
att_rr
att_or
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
같은 모형에서 `comparison` 인수만 바꾸어 **위험차, 위험비, 오즈비**를 모두 구합니다.
:::

## Step 5 · Risk ratio and odds ratio · Results · 결과

```{r}
#| label: effect-rr-out
#| echo: false
att_rr
att_or
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- **Risk ratio = `r sprintf("%.2f", att_rr$estimate)`** (95% CI `r sprintf("%.2f", att_rr$conf.low)`–`r sprintf("%.2f", att_rr$conf.high)`): matched RHC patients had a **`r round(100 * (att_rr$estimate - 1))`% higher** risk of death.
- **Odds ratio = `r sprintf("%.2f", att_or$estimate)`** (95% CI `r sprintf("%.2f", att_or$conf.low)`–`r sprintf("%.2f", att_or$conf.high)`). As expected for a common outcome, it is further from 1 than the RR.
- `lm()` works here because the model contains only `treat`: it predicts each group's observed death rate. With covariates, use a logistic `glm()` for RR and OR, since a linear model can predict risks outside 0–1.
- RD and RR agree: control risk ≈ `r percent(mean(md$died30[md$treat == 0]), 1)`, and `r round(100 * (att_rr$estimate - 1))`% of `r percent(mean(md$died30[md$treat == 0]), 1)` ≈ `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * att_rd$estimate)` percentage points.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**위험비** `r sprintf("%.2f", att_rr$estimate)` (상대적으로 `r round(100 * (att_rr$estimate - 1))`% 높은 위험), **오즈비** `r sprintf("%.2f", att_or$estimate)`. 사망이 흔하므로 오즈비가 위험비보다 1에서 더 멉니다.
:::

## Step 5 · Comparison with Connors et al. · 원 연구와 비교

| | Connors et al. 1996 | Our analysis |
|---|---|---|
| Matching | Propensity score case-matching | Nearest neighbour, caliper 0.2 |
| Matched pairs | 1,006 | `r format(nrow(md) / 2, big.mark = ",")` |
| **30-day mortality, odds ratio (95% CI)** | **1.24 (1.03–1.49)** | **`r sprintf("%.2f (%.2f–%.2f)", att_or$estimate, att_or$conf.low, att_or$conf.high)`** |

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- Our odds ratio is **similar** to the published 1.24, and both CIs exclude 1.
- Connors et al. used a stricter matching procedure (fewer pairs), so the estimates are not identical, but the conclusion is the same: RHC was associated with **higher** 30-day mortality.
- Our CI is narrower because we kept more pairs.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
우리 결과(오즈비 `r sprintf("%.2f", att_or$estimate)`)는 원 연구(오즈비 1.24)와 비슷합니다. 두 분석 모두 RHC와 **높은 30일 사망률**의 연관성을 보였습니다.
:::

## Step 5 · Putting it into words · 결과 서술

| Measure | Estimand | Estimate (95% CI) |
|---|---|---|
| Crude risk difference | association | `r sprintf("%.1f (%.1f to %.1f)", 100*crude$estimate, 100*crude$conf.low, 100*crude$conf.high)` percentage points |
| **Matched risk difference** | ATT | **`r sprintf("%.1f (%.1f to %.1f)", 100*att_rd$estimate, 100*att_rd$conf.low, 100*att_rd$conf.high)` percentage points** |
| **Matched risk ratio** | ATT | **`r sprintf("%.2f (%.2f to %.2f)", att_rr$estimate, att_rr$conf.low, att_rr$conf.high)`** |

> "Among RHC patients for whom a comparable control could be found, RHC within 24 hours was associated with a `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * att_rd$estimate)` percentage-point higher 30-day mortality (95% CI `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * att_rd$conf.low)` to `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * att_rd$conf.high)`; risk ratio `r sprintf("%.2f", att_rr$estimate)`)."

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- Use **"associated with"**, not "caused". The results **suggest** that RHC may increase 30-day mortality, but this is an observational study.
- A causal interpretation rests on assumptions we **cannot verify** from the data: no unmeasured confounding, positivity, and consistency. The sensitivity analysis (E-value) helps judge how fragile the conclusion is.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
RHC는 30일 사망 위험 증가와 **연관**되었습니다 (`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * att_rd$estimate)`%p). 이는 인과적 효과를 **시사**하지만, 검증할 수 없는 가정에 의존하므로 단정할 수 없습니다.
:::

## Step 5 · Doubly robust estimate · 이중 강건 추정

**Doubly robust estimation** combines two adjustments: matching (based on the PS model) **and** an outcome model that includes the covariates. If **at least one** of the two models is correctly specified, the estimate is consistent (approximately unbiased in large samples). It also reduces remaining imbalance in **measured** covariates, but does **not** protect against **unmeasured** confounding.

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (4 min)"}
1. Repeat the risk-difference model, adding all 50 covariates. Save the result as `att_dr`.
2. Compare with `att_rd`: does the estimate change? Is the CI narrower?
:::

```{r}
#| label: dr
#| output: false
fit_dr <- lm(reformulate(c("treat", covs), "died30"), data = md, weights = weights)
att_dr <- avg_comparisons(fit_dr, variables = "treat", vcov = ~subclass,
                          newdata = subset(md, treat == 1))
att_dr
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**이중 강건 추정**: 매칭(성향점수 모형)과 공변량을 포함한 결과모형을 함께 사용합니다. 두 모형 중 **하나만** 올바르게 지정되어도 추정치는 일치성을 가집니다(대표본에서 거의 비편향). **측정되지 않은** 교란은 해결하지 못합니다.
:::

## Step 5 · Doubly robust · Results · 결과

| Analysis | ATT risk difference, percentage points (95% CI) |
|---|---|
| Matching alone (`att_rd`) | `r sprintf("%.1f (%.1f to %.1f)", 100*att_rd$estimate, 100*att_rd$conf.low, 100*att_rd$conf.high)` |
| Matching + covariates in the outcome model (`att_dr`) | `r sprintf("%.1f (%.1f to %.1f)", 100*att_dr$estimate, 100*att_dr$conf.low, 100*att_dr$conf.high)` |

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- **Doubly robust:** nearly the same estimate → the small leftover imbalance in measured covariates did not matter. The CI is slightly **narrower**, because the covariates explain some of the variation in death.
- Agreement between the two analyses makes the result more credible, but none of them addresses **unmeasured** confounding.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
두 분석의 결과가 거의 같습니다 → 남은 작은 불균형은 결과에 큰 영향이 없었습니다. 측정되지 않은 교란은 여전히 남아 있습니다.
:::

# Step 6 · Inverse probability of treatment weighting (IPTW) {background-color="#44475a"}

역확률 처치 가중치 — 매칭의 대안

## IPTW: the idea · 기본 개념

Matching **discards** patients. IPTW **keeps everyone** and gives each patient a weight:

$$
w = \begin{cases} 1 / \text{PS} & \text{if treated} \\ 1 / (1 - \text{PS}) & \text{if untreated} \end{cases}
$$

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
**Why it works · 원리**

- A treated patient with a **low** PS is unusual, so gets a **large** weight: they represent the many similar patients who were not treated.
- The same applies to untreated patients with a high PS.
- The weighted sample is a **pseudo-population** in which treatment no longer depends on the covariates — as if randomized.
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
**Weights and estimands · 추정 대상**

| Weights | Estimand |
|---|---|
| treated 1/PS; untreated 1/(1−PS) | **ATE** |
| treated 1; untreated PS/(1−PS) | **ATT** |
:::
::::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**IPTW**: 환자를 버리지 않고 치료받을 확률의 **역수**로 가중치를 줍니다. 가중된 "가상 집단"에서는 치료가 공변량과 무관해집니다.
:::

## IPTW: a worked example · 계산 예시

16 patients: 8 **mild**, 8 **severe**. Severe patients are more often treated (PS 0.75 vs 0.25).

```{r}
#| label: ipw-toy
#| echo: false
toy <- tibble(
  Severity = c("Mild", "Mild", "Severe", "Severe"),
  Group = c("Treated", "Untreated", "Treated", "Untreated"),
  `Patients (n)` = c(2, 6, 6, 2),
  PS = c(0.25, 0.25, 0.75, 0.75)) |>
  mutate(Weight = if_else(Group == "Treated", 1 / PS, 1 / (1 - PS)),
         `Weighted n` = `Patients (n)` * Weight)
toy |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(c(PS, Weight), decimals = 2) |>
  fmt_number(`Weighted n`, decimals = 0) |>
  tab_style(style = cell_text(color = "#50fa7b", weight = "bold"),
            locations = cells_body(columns = `Weighted n`))
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- **Before weighting:** treated = 2 mild + 6 severe (75% severe); untreated = 6 mild + 2 severe (25% severe) → confounded.
- **Weights:** a mild treated patient is rare (PS 0.25), so gets weight 1/0.25 = **4**; a mild untreated patient is common, so gets 1/0.75 = **1.33**. The reverse holds for severe patients.
- **After weighting:** both groups contain **8 mild + 8 severe**. Severity is balanced, and each group resembles the whole population → comparing them estimates the **ATE**.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
드물게 치료받은 환자는 큰 가중치(4), 흔한 환자는 작은 가중치(1.33)를 받습니다. 가중 후 두 군 모두 **경증 8 + 중증 8**이 됩니다.
:::

## IPTW 1 · Compute the weights · 가중치 계산

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (5 min)"}
1. Using `rhc$ps`, create **ATE weights** `w_ate` (formula on the previous slides).
2. Summarize the weights. What is the largest?
3. Plot a histogram of the weights by treatment group. Save as `p_w`. *(a log-scale x-axis helps)*
:::

```{r}
#| label: iptw-weights
#| output: false
rhc <- rhc |> mutate(w_ate = if_else(treat == 1, 1 / ps, 1 / (1 - ps)))
summary(rhc$w_ate)

p_w <- ggplot(rhc, aes(w_ate, fill = swang1)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 50, alpha = 0.7, position = "identity") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(x = "ATE weight (log scale)", y = "Number of patients", fill = NULL,
       title = "Distribution of IPTW weights")
p_w
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
치료군은 1/PS, 비치료군은 1/(1−PS)로 **ATE 가중치**를 계산합니다.
:::

## IPTW 1 · Weights · Results · 결과

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="58%"}
```{r}
#| label: iptw-weights-plot
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 3.2
p_w
```
:::
::: {.column width="42%"}
```{r}
#| label: iptw-weights-out
#| echo: false
round(summary(rhc$w_ate), 2)
```
:::
::::

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- Weights are always ≥ 1. The median is **`r sprintf("%.2f", median(rhc$w_ate))`**; the largest is **`r sprintf("%.1f", max(rhc$w_ate))`** — one patient counts as about `r round(max(rhc$w_ate))` patients.
- Large weights belong to patients whose treatment was **unexpected** given their PS.
- A few very large weights make estimates **unstable**; we try remedies in IPTW 5.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
가중치가 **너무 큰 환자**가 있으면 추정이 불안정해집니다. 최대 가중치를 항상 확인하세요.
:::

## IPTW 2 · Check balance · 균형 확인

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (5 min)"}
1. Compute the SMDs of all covariates, unweighted and weighted with `w_ate`, with a 0.1 threshold. Save as `bal_ipw`. *(`bal.tab()` with its `weights` argument)*
2. How many terms are balanced after weighting?
3. Draw a Love plot from `bal_ipw`. Save as `p_love_ipw`.
:::

```{r}
#| label: iptw-balance
#| output: false
bal_ipw <- bal.tab(rhc[, covs], treat = rhc$treat, weights = rhc$w_ate,
                   s.d.denom = "pooled", binary = "std",
                   thresholds = c(m = 0.1), un = TRUE)
bal_ipw$Balanced.mean.diffs

p_love_ipw <- love.plot(bal_ipw, abs = TRUE, thresholds = c(m = 0.1),
                        var.order = "unadjusted",
                        colors = c("#ff5555", "#50fa7b"), shapes = c(16, 17),
                        sample.names = c("Unweighted", "IPTW"))
p_love_ipw
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
가중 후에도 모든 공변량의 균형을 확인합니다.
:::

```{r}
#| label: iptw-love-out
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 6.5
#| fig-height: 5.9
love_top(bal_ipw, labels = c("Unweighted", "IPTW"))
```

```{r}
bal_ipw$Balanced.mean.diffs
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- The plot shows the 25 most imbalanced terms (your plot shows all 70). Red = unweighted, green = IPTW.
- After weighting, **`r sum(bal_ipw$Balance$M.Threshold == "Balanced, <0.1", na.rm = TRUE)` of `r nrow(bal_ipw$Balance)`** terms are balanced; the largest |SMD| is **`r sprintf("%.3f", max(abs(bal_ipw$Balance$Diff.Adj)))`**.
- IPTW balanced the covariates **without discarding anyone**.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
IPTW 후 모든 |SMD| < 0.1 → 환자를 버리지 않고 균형을 맞췄습니다.
:::
:::
::::

## IPTW 3 · Weighted Table 1 · 가중 기초특성표

1. Create a **survey design** object that carries the weights. *(survey: `svydesign()`)*
2. Make the same Table 1 as before, now weighted, with p-values and SMDs. Save as `tbl_ipw`. *(gtsummary: `tbl_svysummary()`, `add_p()`, `add_smd()`)*

```{r}
#| label: iptw-table

iptw_design <- svydesign(ids = ~1, weights = ~w_ate, data = rhc)
tbl_ipw <- tbl_svysummary(iptw_design, by = swang1, include = all_of(key_vars),
                          label = var_labels,
                          statistic = all_continuous() ~ "{mean} ({sd})") |>
  add_p() |>
  add_smd() |>
  bold_labels()
```

## IPTW 3 · Weighted Table 1 · Results · 결과

```{r}
#| label: iptw-table-out
#| echo: false
tbl_ipw
```

## IPTW 3 · Weighted Table 1 · Interpretation · 해석

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- Numbers are now **weighted** "pseudo-patients": about `r format(round(sum(rhc$w_ate[rhc$treat == 0]), -2), big.mark = ",")` without RHC and `r format(round(sum(rhc$w_ate[rhc$treat == 1]), -2), big.mark = ",")` with RHC — each close to the full cohort of `r format(nrow(rhc), big.mark = ",")`, because the ATE compares the whole cohort treated vs the whole cohort untreated.
- p-values here come from survey-weighted tests; all are large, but as before we judge balance by the SMD.
- Both groups now resemble the **whole cohort**: e.g., APACHE III ≈ `r round(weighted.mean(rhc$aps1[rhc$treat == 1], rhc$w_ate[rhc$treat == 1]))` in each (cohort mean `r round(mean(rhc$aps1))`), and every |SMD| < 0.1.
- After **matching**, both groups resembled the **RHC patients** (ATT). After **IPTW**, both resemble **everyone** (ATE).
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
IPTW 후 두 군은 **전체 코호트**와 비슷해집니다 (ATE). 매칭 후에는 **RHC 환자**와 비슷했습니다 (ATT).
:::

## IPTW 4 · Estimate the ATE · 평균처치효과 추정

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (5 min)"}
1. Estimate the **ATE risk difference**: a weighted linear model of `died30` on `treat` in the full data, then `avg_comparisons()`. Save as `ate_rd`.
2. Estimate the **ATE risk ratio** the same way with a weighted `glm()` (`family = quasibinomial()`: same estimates as `binomial()`, but no warning about non-integer weights). Save as `ate_rr`.
:::

::: {.callout-warning title="💡 Hint · 힌트"}
There are no pairs, so use robust standard errors (`vcov = "HC3"`) instead of `~subclass`, and leave out `newdata` so the effect is averaged over **all** patients.
:::

```{r}
#| label: iptw-effect
#| output: false
fit_ipw <- lm(died30 ~ treat, data = rhc, weights = w_ate)
ate_rd  <- avg_comparisons(fit_ipw, variables = "treat", vcov = "HC3")

fit_ipw_log <- glm(died30 ~ treat, data = rhc, weights = w_ate, family = quasibinomial())
ate_rr  <- avg_comparisons(fit_ipw_log, variables = "treat", vcov = "HC3",
                           comparison = "lnratioavg", transform = "exp")
ate_rd
ate_rr
```

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
가중 모형으로 **ATE** 위험차와 위험비를 추정합니다.
:::

## IPTW 4 · ATE · Results · 결과

```{r}
#| label: iptw-effect-out
#| echo: false
ate_rd
ate_rr
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- **ATE risk difference = `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * ate_rd$estimate)` percentage points** (95% CI `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * ate_rd$conf.low)` to `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * ate_rd$conf.high)`): if **every** patient in the cohort received RHC, 30-day mortality would be about `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * ate_rd$estimate)` points higher than if **none** did.
- **ATE risk ratio = `r sprintf("%.2f", ate_rr$estimate)`** (95% CI `r sprintf("%.2f", ate_rr$conf.low)`–`r sprintf("%.2f", ate_rr$conf.high)`).
- Close to the matched ATT (RD `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * att_rd$estimate)`, RR `r sprintf("%.2f", att_rr$estimate)`), although it answers a different question.
- These robust SEs ignore that the PS was estimated, so the CI is usually slightly too wide (conservative).
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**ATE**: 모든 환자가 RHC를 받은 경우 vs 아무도 받지 않은 경우, 30일 사망 위험이 `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * ate_rd$estimate)`%p 높습니다 (위험비 `r sprintf("%.2f", ate_rr$estimate)`).
:::

## IPTW 5 · Variations on the weights · 가중치 변형

Three common variations. The code is longer, so it is shown in full — **run it and compare the results**.

- **Stabilized ATE weights** `w_stab`: multiply each weight by the overall proportion treated (treated patients) or untreated (untreated patients) → same estimate, smaller extreme weights
- **Trimmed ATE weights** `w_trim`: cap the weights at their 99th percentile
- **ATT weights** `w_att`: 1 for treated, PS/(1 − PS) for untreated; average over treated patients only

```{r}
#| label: iptw-variants
#| output: false
#| code-fold: false
p_treat <- mean(rhc$treat)
rhc <- rhc |>
  mutate(w_stab = if_else(treat == 1, p_treat / ps, (1 - p_treat) / (1 - ps)),
         w_trim = pmin(w_ate, quantile(w_ate, 0.99)),
         w_att  = if_else(treat == 1, 1, ps / (1 - ps)))

rd_with <- function(w, att = FALSE) {
  f  <- lm(died30 ~ treat, data = rhc, weights = rhc[[w]])
  nd <- if (att) subset(rhc, treat == 1) else rhc
  avg_comparisons(f, variables = "treat", vcov = "HC3", newdata = nd)
}
ipw_variants <- tibble(
  weights  = c("w_ate", "w_stab", "w_trim", "w_att"),
  estimand = c("ATE", "ATE", "ATE (trimmed)", "ATT"),
  max_w    = map_dbl(weights, \(w) max(rhc[[w]])),
  res      = map2(weights, estimand == "ATT", rd_with)) |>
  mutate(rd = map_dbl(res, "estimate"), lo = map_dbl(res, "conf.low"),
         hi = map_dbl(res, "conf.high")) |>
  select(-res)
ipw_variants
```

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (5 min)"}
Run the code. Which weights have the largest maximum weight? Do the risk differences differ?
:::

## IPTW 5 · Variations · Results · 결과

```{r}
#| label: iptw-variants-out
#| echo: false
ipw_variants |>
  mutate(across(c(rd, lo, hi), \(x) 100 * x)) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(max_w, decimals = 1) |>
  fmt_number(c(rd, lo, hi), decimals = 1) |>
  cols_merge(c(lo, hi), pattern = "{1} to {2}") |>
  cols_label(weights = "Weights", estimand = "Estimand", max_w = "Largest weight",
             rd = "Risk difference (pp)", lo = "95% CI")
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- **Stabilized:** the same estimate as ordinary ATE weights, with a much smaller largest weight. In more complex models this gives more stable results.
- **Trimmed:** the estimate changes only slightly → the extreme weights were not driving the result.
- **ATT weights:** `r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * ipw_variants$rd[ipw_variants$weights == "w_att"])` percentage points, similar to the matched ATT (`r sprintf("%.1f", 100 * att_rd$estimate)`): two methods, the same estimand, similar answers.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**안정화 가중치**는 추정치는 같고 극단값이 작습니다. **절단**해도 결과가 비슷하고, **ATT 가중치** 결과는 매칭 결과와 비슷합니다.
:::

# Comparing methods & sensitivity analysis {background-color="#44475a"}

방법 비교와 민감도 분석

## Comparing approaches · 방법 비교

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (6 min)"}
1. Estimate the ATE with an **outcome regression**: a logistic model of `died30` on `treat` and all 50 covariates in the full data, then `avg_comparisons()`. Save as `adj`.
2. Collect the risk differences from `crude`, `adj`, `att_rd`, `att_dr`, and `ate_rd` in one data frame.
3. Draw a **forest plot**: one point and 95% CI per method, with a line at 0. Save as `p_forest`. *(`geom_point()`, `geom_errorbarh()`)*
:::

```{r}
#| label: compare
#| output: false
adj_fit <- glm(reformulate(c("treat", covs), "died30"), family = binomial, data = rhc)
adj     <- avg_comparisons(adj_fit, variables = "treat", vcov = "HC3")

res <- bind_rows(
  tibble(method = "Crude (no adjustment)",       est = crude$estimate,  lo = crude$conf.low,  hi = crude$conf.high),
  tibble(method = "Outcome regression (ATE)",    est = adj$estimate,    lo = adj$conf.low,    hi = adj$conf.high),
  tibble(method = "PS matching (ATT)",           est = att_rd$estimate, lo = att_rd$conf.low, hi = att_rd$conf.high),
  tibble(method = "Matching + regression (ATT)", est = att_dr$estimate, lo = att_dr$conf.low, hi = att_dr$conf.high),
  tibble(method = "IPTW (ATE)",                  est = ate_rd$estimate, lo = ate_rd$conf.low, hi = ate_rd$conf.high)
) |>
  mutate(across(c(est, lo, hi), \(x) 100 * x),
         method = fct_rev(fct_inorder(method)))

p_forest <- ggplot(res, aes(est, method)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = 2, colour = "grey60") +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = 0.2, colour = "#8be9fd") +
  geom_point(size = 3.5, colour = "#ff79c6") +
  labs(x = "Risk difference, 30-day mortality (percentage points)", y = NULL,
       title = "RHC and 30-day mortality: five estimates")
p_forest
```

## Comparing approaches · Results · 결과

```{r}
#| label: forest-out
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.4
p_forest
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- Each point is a risk difference; each line is its 95% CI; the dashed line is 0 (no effect).
- All adjusted estimates (`r sprintf("%.1f to %.1f", min(res$est[-1]), max(res$est[-1]))` points) are **smaller** than the crude estimate (`r sprintf("%.1f", res$est[1])`): part of the crude difference was confounding by severity.
- All CIs exclude 0, and all point the same way: **no sign of benefit, and likely harm**.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
보정한 결과는 모두 단순 비교보다 작지만, 모두 **같은 방향**(사망 위험 증가)을 가리킵니다.
:::

## Comparing approaches · Table · 결과표

```{r}
#| label: compare-tab
#| echo: false
res |>
  arrange(desc(method)) |>
  mutate(method = as.character(method)) |>
  gt() |>
  fmt_number(c(est, lo, hi), decimals = 1) |>
  cols_merge(c(lo, hi), pattern = "{1} to {2}") |>
  cols_label(method = "Method", est = "Risk difference (pp)", lo = "95% CI")
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- **Outcome regression** and **IPTW** estimate the **ATE** (whole cohort); **matching** estimates the **ATT** (matchable RHC patients). Small differences are expected because they answer different questions.
- These methods rely on different models (outcome model vs PS model). Their agreement is reassuring — but none of them can remove **unmeasured** confounding.
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
서로 다른 모형에 기반한 방법들의 결과가 비슷하면 결론에 더 확신을 가질 수 있습니다. 단, **측정되지 않은 교란**은 해결하지 못합니다.
:::

## Sensitivity analysis: the E-value · 민감도 분석

How strong would an **unmeasured confounder** have to be to explain away our result?

$$
E = RR + \sqrt{RR \times (RR - 1)}
$$

The E-value is the minimum risk ratio that an unmeasured confounder would need with **both** RHC **and** death — beyond the measured covariates — to fully explain the observed association.

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Your turn · 직접 해보기 (5 min)"}
1. Compute the E-value for the **matched risk ratio** `att_rr` (estimate and CI). Save as `ev`. *(EValue: `evalues.RR()`)*
2. Do the same for the **crude** risk ratio (get it from `crude_fit` with `comparison = "lnratioavg"`, as in Step 5).
:::

```{r}
#| label: evalue
#| output: false
ev <- evalues.RR(est = att_rr$estimate, lo = att_rr$conf.low, hi = att_rr$conf.high)
ev

crude_rr <- avg_comparisons(crude_fit, variables = "treat", vcov = "HC3",
                            comparison = "lnratioavg", transform = "exp")
ev_crude <- evalues.RR(est = crude_rr$estimate, lo = crude_rr$conf.low, hi = crude_rr$conf.high)
ev_crude
```

## E-value · Results · 결과

```{r}
#| label: evalue-out
#| echo: false
ev
ev_crude
```

::: {.callout-note title="🔎 Interpretation · 해석"}
- **Matched RR `r sprintf("%.2f", att_rr$estimate)`:** E-value (`point`) = **`r sprintf("%.2f", ev["E-values", "point"])`**. An unmeasured confounder associated with both RHC and death by a risk ratio of `r sprintf("%.2f", ev["E-values", "point"])` **each** could fully explain the association. For the CI limit (`lower`): **`r sprintf("%.2f", ev["E-values", "lower"])`** would be enough to make the CI include 1. (`upper` is `NA`: only the limit nearer 1 matters.)
- **Crude RR `r sprintf("%.2f", crude_rr$estimate)`:** E-value `r sprintf("%.2f", ev_crude["E-values", "point"])`.
- Is a confounder of strength ≈ `r sprintf("%.1f", ev["E-values", "point"])` plausible? A doctor's bedside impression of how sick a patient is might be that strong → the evidence for **harm** is moderate. (Connors et al.'s sensitivity analysis asked a different question: a hidden confounder would need to raise both RHC use and death about 6-fold to make a truly *beneficial* RHC look harmful.)
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
**E-값** `r sprintf("%.2f", ev["E-values", "point"])`: 측정되지 않은 교란변수가 RHC와 사망 **모두와** 위험비 `r sprintf("%.2f", ev["E-values", "point"])` 이상으로 연관되어야 결과를 설명할 수 있습니다. 클수록 **견고**합니다.
:::

## EHR-specific pitfalls · EHR 자료의 함정

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Missing data · 결측치**

- Labs are ordered *because* a doctor was worried → missingness carries information
- Consider multiple imputation (e.g., `mice` with `MatchThem`)

**Time · 시간**

- Define **time zero** clearly (e.g., ICU admission)
- Covariates **before** time zero, outcome **after**
- Avoid **immortal time bias**
:::
::: {.column width="50%"}
**Measurement · 측정**

- Diagnosis codes ≠ disease
- "No code" ≠ "no disease"

**Design · 설계**

- **Target trial emulation**: write the protocol of the trial you wish you had, then emulate it with EHR data
- **New-user, active-comparator** designs
:::
::::

::: {.callout-tip title="🧑‍💻 Discuss · 토론 (3 min)"}
Write a 5-line **target trial protocol** for the RHC question: eligibility, treatment strategies, time zero, outcome, follow-up. Which element is hardest to define with EHR data?
:::

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
실제 EHR 연구에서는 **결측치, 시간 정의(time zero), 코드 오분류**가 성향점수 모형보다 더 큰 문제일 수 있습니다.
:::

## Reporting checklist · 보고 체크리스트

| Report | 보고 항목 |
|---|---|
| Question, time zero, estimand (ATT / ATE) | 연구 질문·추정 대상 |
| Covariates and why they were chosen | 공변량 선택 근거 |
| PS model and overlap plot | 성향점수 모형·중첩 그래프 |
| Matching method, ratio, caliper, replacement | 매칭 방법 |
| Number matched and unmatched | 매칭/미매칭 수 |
| Table 1 with SMD before and after; Love plot | 매칭 전후 균형 |
| Effect estimates (RD, RR), 95% CI, SE method | 효과 추정치 |
| Sensitivity analyses (IPTW, doubly robust, E-value) | 민감도 분석 |
| Handling of missing data | 결측치 처리 |

Reviewers look first at the **balance table** and the **number of matched patients** · 리뷰어는 **균형표**와 **매칭된 환자 수**를 가장 먼저 봅니다.

## Key takeaways · 핵심 요약

1. In EHR data, treatment is **not random** → confounding by indication · 치료는 무작위가 아니다
2. A **propensity score** summarizes many covariates in one number · 성향점수 = 치료받을 확률
3. **Design first, outcome last** · 설계 먼저, 결과는 마지막
4. Judge the PS model by **balance (|SMD| < 0.1)**, not p-values · 균형으로 평가
5. Know your **estimand**: matching → ATT; IPTW → ATE · 추정 대상을 명확히
6. Report the **risk difference and the risk ratio** · 위험차와 위험비 모두 보고
7. PS methods **cannot fix unmeasured confounding** → sensitivity analysis · 측정되지 않은 교란은 해결 불가

::: {.callout-caution title="🇰🇷 핵심"}
성향점수 방법은 관찰연구를 **무작위 시험처럼 설계**하려는 도구입니다. 가정과 한계를 함께 보고하세요.
:::
